tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

1	# Yamark
2	
3	Yamark is a fast formatter for YAML and Markdown. It formats whole files and embedded content, keeping source readable and changes easy to review. Regions without a supported rewrite stay unchanged.
4	
5	For supported embedded code, Yamark can also call Ruff, Air, Prettier, or another configured formatter.
6	
7	See the [documentation](https://t-kalinowski.github.io/yamark/) for examples, configuration, editor integrations, and the full syntax reference.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed, run Yamark directly from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/yamark/) without a separate install:
12	
13	```sh
14	uvx yamark format config.yaml docs/
15	```
16	
17	This formats the selected files in place. To install a persistent `yamark` command:
18	
19	```sh
20	uv tool install yamark
21	```
22	
23	## Usage
24	
25	The examples below use an installed `yamark` command. To keep running from PyPI without installing it, replace `yamark` with `uvx yamark`.
26	
27	Format one or more files or directories in place:
28	
29	```sh
30	yamark format config.yaml docs/
31	```
32	
33	Format the current directory:
34	
35	```sh
36	yamark format
37	```
38	
39	Check whether files are already formatted without writing changes:
40	
41	```sh
42	yamark format --check docs/
43	```
44	
45	Show a unified diff without writing changes:
46	
47	```sh
48	yamark format --diff docs/
49	```
50	
51	Format stdin for editor and CI integrations:
52	
53	```sh
54	yamark format --stdin-file-path config.yaml < config.yaml
55	```
56	
57	Convert JSON-family input from stdin to formatted YAML on stdout:
58	
59	```sh
60	yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json5 < data.json5
61	```
62	
63	The path is not read or written. Its suffix selects the exact JSON dialect. This is a conversion, not source formatting.
64	
65	Directory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and global Git ignore files by default. Pass a hidden path explicitly to format it.
66	
67	While formatting is enabled, standalone `{{< ... >}}` and `{{% ... %}}` shortcode tokens are preserved, including multiline tokens and quoted arguments. Directive-looking text inside a recognized token is data. Yamark does not match shortcode names or interpret their bodies: Markdown between tokens formats normally. An unterminated token or quote preserves the rest of the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This does not guarantee rendering equivalence for arbitrary Hugo or Jinja templates.
68	
69	To disable body formatting, surround the region with `<!-- fmt: off -->` and `<!-- fmt: on -->`. While formatting is disabled, directives follow the existing linewise policy: a recognized `fmt: on` line resumes formatting even if the surrounding text resembles a shortcode argument, code fence, HTML, or math block.
70	
71	Explicitly skipped Markdown retains its bytes, including trailing spaces and line endings: `<!-- fmt: skip -->` preserves the next selected node, `<!-- fmt: off -->` preserves the disabled region, and `<!-- fmt: skip file -->` preserves the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This protection survives supported nesting in Markdown fences and divs; surrounding Markdown still formats.
72	
73	## Editor integrations
74	
75	The VS Code and Positron formatter extension lives in `editors/vscode/`. See the [editor guide][editor-docs] for installation and configuration.
76	
77

1	---
2	# fmt: skip file
3	title: Directives
4	description: Tell Yamark what to format, skip, preserve, or configure from inside the file.
5	---
6	
7	<!-- fmt: skip file -->
8	
9	The source file is the primary interface. Put a small `fmt:` directive next to
10	the text it controls, then let an editor or repository integration run Yamark.
11	Because directives are comments, the formatting choice stays with the text.
12	The comment marker depends on the file:
13	
14	| File | Directive comment |
15	| --- | --- |
16	| Markdown and Quarto | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` |
17	| YAML, Python, and R | `# fmt: ...` |
18	
19	Quarto chunk options use `#|`; for example, `#| fmt: skip`.
20	
21	## Target the next value or block
22	
23	Most directives apply to the next supported target. In a YAML file, that target
24	is usually a scalar node. In a Python or R file, it is usually a string literal
25	or a contiguous source-comment block. The directive does not format the
26	surrounding Python or R source code.
27	
28	## YAML files
29	
30	Mark a scalar as Markdown and choose sentence wrapping for that scalar:
31	
32	```yaml
33	# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
34	description: "Explain the project in a few clear sentences."
35	other_value: "This is ordinary YAML, not Markdown."
36	```
37	
38	The directive attaches to `description`, the next scalar. A tagged scalar is
39	another way to mark Markdown when the setting should travel with the value:
40	
41	```yaml
42	instructions: !markdown |
43	  # Review
44	
45	  Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues.
46	```
47	
48	Use the same placement for an embedded formatter. The formatter name is the
49	language after `fmt:`:
50	
51	```yaml
52	# fmt: python
53	script: |
54	  def check(items):return all(item > 0 for item in items)
55	```
56	
57	YAML also supports directives on a collection parent when the setting describes
58	the collection rather than a scalar:
59	
60	```yaml
61	# fmt: table
62	- {name: alpha, type: string, default: ""}
63	- {name: beta, type: integer, default: 0}
64	```
65	
66	## Python files
67	
68	Put `# fmt: markdown` immediately before the string literal or comment block
69	that contains Markdown:
70	
71	```python
72	# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
73	REVIEW_PROMPT = """
74	# Review
75	
76	Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues. Prefer specific examples.
77	"""
78	```
79	
80	The `#` lines inside the string are Markdown content. Python outside the
81	marked target is left for a Python formatter such as Ruff.
82	
83	The same directive can target a Markdown comment block:
84	
85	```python
86	# fmt: markdown
87	# # Filters
88	#
89	# Apply the most specific filter first.
90	#
91	# - Each filter is a single expression.
92	```
93	
94	For a non-Markdown embedded language, use its formatter name:
95	
96	```python
97	# fmt: r
98	analysis = """
99	f <- function(x) x + 1
100	"""
101	```
102	
103	## R files
104	
105	R uses the same `# fmt:` marker. It can target a raw string literal used for a
106	vignette, help text, or a Shiny message:
107	
108	```r
109	# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
110	help_text <- r"(
111	# Filters
112	
113	Apply the most specific filter first. Explain why a filter matched.
114	)"
115	```
116	
117	It can also target a contiguous Markdown comment block:
118	
119	```r
120	# fmt: markdown
121	# # Filters
122	#
123	# Apply the most specific filter first.
124	#
125	# - Each filter is a single expression.
126	```
127	
128	For source code inside a YAML literal scalar, use the language formatter name
129	in the same way as in a YAML file:
130	
131	```yaml
132	# fmt: r
133	analysis: |
134	  f <- function(x)x+1
135	```
136	
137	## Control a region or a whole file
138	
139	The scope is part of the directive. `next` is the default for target directives.
140	Use `from-here` for the rest of a region, and `file` for a document-wide
141	setting:
142	
143	| Scope | Applies to |
144	| --- | --- |
145	| `scope=next` | The next supported string, scalar, collection, or comment block. |
146	| `scope=from-here` | Supported content from this point until another directive changes the setting. |
147	| `scope=file` | The whole file, including supported content before the directive. |
148	
149	Skip one target:
150	
151	```yaml
152	normal: [1, 2, 3]
153	# fmt: skip
154	manual:
155	    -   [ 1,2,3]
156	```
157	
158	Preserve a region and resume formatting afterward:
159	
160	```markdown
161	<!-- fmt: off -->
162	#   Keep this heading ##
163	
164	<!-- fmt: on -->
165	```
166	
167	Skip a whole file by putting the file directive at the top. YAML, Python, and R
168	use the same hash-comment form:
169	
170	```text
171	# fmt: skip file
172	```
173	
174	Markdown uses an HTML comment:
175	
176	```markdown
177	<!-- fmt: skip file -->
178	```
179	
180	A whole-file skip is useful for generated files or files whose layout is
181	intentionally outside Yamark's scope.
182	
183	Markdown skip controls retain trailing spaces and line endings in the selected
184	content, including supported nested Markdown.
185	
186	## Preserve intentional table widths
187	
188	Yamark normally fits table columns to their contents. Keep a table's authored
189	widths while still formatting its contents:
190	
191	```markdown
192	<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->
193	+----------+------------------+
194	| Name     | Description      |
195	+==========+==================+
196	| A        | Short text       |
197	+----------+------------------+
198	```
199	
200	Use `scope=file` to preserve widths throughout the document, or
201	`scope=from-here` for subsequent tables. A later
202	`table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths. Both modes retain
203	column alignment. Fitting widths can change the rendered proportions of
204	Pandoc tables; preserving widths can retain excessive or cramped padding.
205	
206	For Markdown inside YAML, Python, or R, the same option can accompany the
207	target marker: `# fmt: markdown table-widths=preserve`.
208	
209	## Set file-specific Markdown options
210	
211	Use `scope=file` when the file should have a different Markdown policy from the
212	repository default:
213	
214	```markdown
215	<!-- fmt: wrap=sentence:72 scope=file -->
216	```
217	
218	This puts one sentence per line and wraps long sentences at column 72. Other
219	file-wide Markdown options include `canonical=true` and
220	`footnotes=preserve`:
221	
222	```markdown
223	<!-- fmt: canonical=true footnotes=preserve scope=file -->
224	```
225	
226	For a YAML file or a hashpipe YAML stream in Python or R, use the same scope to
227	set YAML behavior for the whole file:
228	
229	```yaml
230	# fmt: compact=false scope=file
231	```
232	
233	An option-only directive such as `# fmt: canonical=true` adjusts the next
234	already-marked Markdown scalar. It does not turn an ordinary YAML scalar into a
235	Markdown target:
236	
237	```yaml
238	# fmt: canonical=true
239	first: !markdown "This is __strong__ Markdown."
240	second: "This is ordinary YAML text."
241	```
242	
243	## Arrange for Yamark to run automatically
244	
245	Once directives are in the files, configure Yamark to run as part of the
246	workflow:
247	
248	- In an editor, enable format on save. The [Editors](editors.qmd) page shows
249	  the VS Code and Positron settings. This is the most direct way to see a
250	  directive take effect while editing.
251	- In a pre-commit hook, run `yamark format`. In CI, use
252	  `yamark format --check` to verify files without changing them.
253	
254	The experimental [Git Filter](git-filter.qmd) serves a narrower workflow: it
255	stores selected Markdown files sentence-per-line while keeping the working tree
256	column-wrapped.
257	
258	## When a repository default is better
259	
260	Use `yamark.toml` for settings that should apply broadly rather than to one
261	piece of text. Keep local exceptions in directives so they stay beside the
262	content they explain.
263	
264	For example, a repository can choose sentence-per-line Markdown and compact
265	YAML collections by default:
266	
267	```toml
268	[format]
269	wrap = "sentence:88"
270	compact = true
271	```
272	
273	Yamark discovers `yamark.toml` from each formatted file's directory upward.
274	Use the [Configuration reference](reference-config.qmd) for the full
275	`[format]`, `[template]`, `[embedded]`, and `[paths]` schema.
276	
277	## For one-off runs
278	
279	Command-line options are useful for trying a policy, checking files in CI, or
280	overriding a repository default for one invocation:
281	
282	```sh
283	yamark format --wrap sentence:72 docs/
284	yamark format --compact config.yaml
285	yamark format --check docs/
286	```
287	
288	Use the [Directive syntax reference](reference-directives.qmd) for every
289	accepted form, scope, and value.
290	
291	Use the [Command-line reference](cli-help.qmd) for the accepted arguments and
292	[Usage](usage.qmd) for installation and common commands.

5	---
6	
7	<!-- fmt: skip file -->
8	
9	Directives are comments whose trimmed content starts with `fmt:`. This page is
10	an exact syntax lookup. For a guided path through YAML, Python, and R examples,
11	see [Directives](directives.qmd).
12	
13	## Comment forms
14	
15	| Host | Form | Placement |
16	| --- | --- | --- |
17	| Markdown | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` | An own-line HTML comment. |
18	| YAML | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment. `fmt: table` and `fmt: compact table` may also be same-line comments on an empty-valued collection parent; a populated parent is an error. |
19	| Python and R | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment before a supported comment or string target. |
20	
21	## Scopes
22	
23	| Scope | Meaning |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| `scope=next` | Apply to the next supported target. This is the default for target-selecting, compact, table, and embedded-formatter directives. |
26	| `scope=from-here` | Apply from the directive until another directive changes the same state. |
27	| `scope=file` | Apply throughout the current parsed document or nested region, including supported nodes before the directive. At the top level, that region is the physical file. |
28	
29	Not every directive accepts every scope. The tables below list the supported
30	forms. An unsupported or misspelled explicit scope is an error. Template
31	delimiter directives use the contextual rule described below instead of one
32	fixed default.
33	
34	Scopes stop at the current parsed document or nested-region boundary. A
35	directive inside a recursive fence affects that fence, not its Markdown host or
36	sibling fences. A `scope=file` directive inside one hashpipe YAML block does not
37	span later blocks. `fmt: skip file` in Markdown front matter is the exception:
38	it preserves the outer Markdown document.
39	
40	## Preserve content
41	
42	| Directive | Scope | Effect |
43	| --- | --- | --- |
44	| `fmt: skip` | Next | Preserve the next supported target. `fmt: skip scope=next` is equivalent. |
45	| `fmt: skip file` | File | Preserve the current parsed document or nested region. `fmt: skip scope=file` is equivalent. |
46	| `fmt: off` | From here | Preserve content until `fmt: on`, or through the end of Markdown and source regions. `fmt: off scope=from-here` is equivalent. |
47	| `fmt: on` | - | Resume formatting after `fmt: off`. It does not accept an explicit scope. |
48	
49	The same control uses the host's comment form:
50	
51	```yaml
52	# fmt: skip
53	manual: [[ 1,2,3], [4,5,6]]
54	```
55	
56	```markdown
57	<!-- fmt: off -->
58	*   keep
59	    this
60	    list
61	<!-- fmt: on -->
62	```
63	
64	Preserve-control lifecycle checks are host-specific. YAML rejects a targetless
65	`skip`, a stray `on`, a nested `off`, and an `off` without a later `on`.
66	Markdown and source regions allow `skip` at the end and let `off` preserve
67	through the end of the region.
68	
69	## Markdown targets and settings
70	
71	| Form | Default scope | Effect |
72	| --- | --- | --- |
73	| `fmt: markdown` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown: a Markdown block, including a supported fence; a YAML scalar; or a source string or comment block. |
74	| `fmt: markdown wrap=sentence canonical=true` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown and set its options. |
75	| `fmt: wrap=sentence` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Change wrapping for an already recognized Markdown region without marking unrelated content. |
76	| `fmt: table-widths=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve widths in supported Markdown tables while formatting contents. Use `scope=next` immediately before one table. |
77	| `fmt: canonical` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Enable canonical Markdown spelling. `canonical=true` is equivalent. |
78	| `fmt: footnotes=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve footnote definitions in the affected Markdown. |
79	
80	Option-only YAML directives tune the next scalar only if it is already marked
81	as Markdown:
82	
83	```yaml
84	# fmt: canonical=true
85	first: !markdown "This is __strong__."
86	second: "This is __not__ Markdown."
87	```
88	
89	For `scope=from-here` or `scope=file`, `fmt: markdown` must include at least one
90	actual Markdown option. A broad-scope directive changes Markdown settings; it
91	does not turn every plain scalar into Markdown.
92	
93	Accepted option values:
94	
95	| Option | Values |
96	| --- | --- |
97	| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer. |
98	| `table-widths` | `fit` (the default) or `preserve`. Both preserve alignment. |
99	| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. A bare `canonical` means `true`. |
100	| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |
101	
102	For `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` request formatting;
103	`preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` request preservation.
104	
105	## YAML collections
106	
107	| Directive | Scope | Effect |
108	| --- | --- | --- |
109	| `fmt: compact` | Next | Enable block-to-flow compaction for the next eligible collection. |
110	| `fmt: compact false` | Next | Disable compaction for the next eligible collection. `fmt: compact=false` is equivalent. |
111	| `fmt: compact scope=from-here` | From here | Enable compaction until another compact directive changes the state. |
112	| `fmt: compact=false scope=file` | File | Disable compaction throughout the current YAML document or one source-file hashpipe YAML block. |
113	| `fmt: table` | Next | Align the next compatible sequence of flow mappings. |
114	| `fmt: compact table` | Next | Collapse eligible block mapping rows before aligning them. `fmt: table compact` and `fmt: table compact=true` are equivalent. |
115	
116	`fmt: table` accepts only its default next-target scope. Compact directives
117	accept `next`, `from-here`, and `file`.
118	
119	`compact`, `compact=true`, `compact=yes`, `compact=1`, and `compact true`
120	enable compaction. `compact=false`, `compact=no`, `compact=0`, and
121	`compact false` disable it. The separated form accepts only `true` or `false`.
122	
123	## Templates and embedded formatters
124	
125	| Directive | Scope | Effect |
126	| --- | --- | --- |
127	| `fmt: template.delimiters "<<" ">>"` | Inferred | Add one non-empty double-quoted delimiter pair using the placement rule below. |
128	| `fmt: template.delimiters "<<" ">>" scope=next` | Next | Add the pair to the next supported target. |
129	| `fmt: template.delimiters "<<" ">>" scope=from-here` | From here | Add the pair to following supported targets. |
130	| `fmt: template.delimiters "<<" ">>" scope=file` | File | Add the pair throughout the current document or nested region. |
131	| `fmt: embedded python` | Next | Format the next supported string or YAML literal scalar with the named formatter. |
132	| `fmt: python` | Next | Shorthand for `fmt: embedded python`. |
133	
134	A bare `fmt: template.delimiters` directive uses the next target when placed
135	directly before one. When blank lines or range boundaries isolate it from
136	content on both sides, it applies from there onward. The directive requires an
137	explicit scope in every other placement.
138	
139	Delimiter arguments must be non-empty double-quoted tokens; single quotes are
140	not accepted. Inside a token, `\"`, `\\`, `\n`, `\r`, and `\t` represent a
141	double quote, backslash, newline, carriage return, and tab.
142	
143	Embedded formatter directives accept only `scope=next`. The name can select a
144	built-in alias or an entry from [`[embedded]`](reference-config.qmd#embedded).
145	
146	YAML can also mark a scalar as Markdown with the `!markdown` or `!md` tag:
147	
148	```yaml
149	body: !markdown "A paragraph with [a link](https://example.com)."
150	```
151	
152	## Source files and fenced chunks
153	
154	| Host | Directive | Effect |
155	| --- | --- | --- |
156	| Python or R comment or string | `fmt: markdown` | Format the next supported comment block or string as Markdown. Surrounding source code stays unchanged. |
157	| Python or R string | `fmt: <name>` or `fmt: embedded <name>` | Format the next supported string with the named embedded formatter. Surrounding source code stays unchanged. |
158	| Markdown fence | An opening attribute such as `` ```yaml fmt: skip `` | Preserve that fence locally. |
159	| Quarto source fence | `#| fmt: skip` anywhere in the initial consecutive `#|` option block | Preserve that chunk locally. |
160	
161	[Supported files and syntax](reference-files.qmd#python-and-r-source-files)
162	describes automatic hashpipe YAML recognition. The [Markdown behavior
163	table](reference-files.qmd#markdown) describes Quarto fence-header promotion.

6	Use this page to determine what Yamark selects and what it does with a specific
7	construct. [Formatting settings](reference-options.qmd) describes how to change
8	the output.
9	
10	## Files and regions
11	
12	| Input | What Yamark formats | Selection |
13	| --- | --- | --- |
14	| `.yaml` and `.yml` | The whole YAML stream. | Automatic for path-aware formatting. |
15	| `.md`, `.qmd`, `.Rmd`, and `.rmd` | Markdown, YAML front matter, and recognized fenced content. | Automatic, except constructs described as preserved below. |
16	| `.py`, `.R`, and `.r` | `#|` hashpipe YAML blocks, marked Markdown comments or strings, and marked external-formatter targets. | Hashpipe blocks are automatic; other targets require a `fmt:` directive. Surrounding source code is unchanged. |
17	| `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.json5`, `.jsonl`, and `.ndjson` | A YAML projection of the whole JSON-family input. | Explicit through `yamark to-yaml` or `Yamark: View JSON as YAML`. Normal formatting does not select these files. |
18	| Markdown fences named `yaml`, `yml`, `markdown`, or `md` | YAML, or recursively formatted Markdown. | Automatic unless the fence is locally skipped. |
19	| Markdown source fences | Python, R, JSON, GraphQL, CSS, HTML, JavaScript, TypeScript, and related aliases. | Delegated when a matching embedded formatter is available. |
20	| YAML scalars tagged `!markdown` or `!md` | The scalar value as Markdown. | Explicit tag. |
21	| YAML scalars following `# fmt: markdown` | The scalar value as Markdown. | Explicit directive. |
22	| YAML literal scalars following `# fmt: <name>` or `# fmt: embedded <name>` | The scalar value through a built-in or configured embedded formatter. | Explicit directive. |
23	
24	Extension matching is ASCII case-insensitive. In path mode, unsupported
25	extensions are counted as skipped and do not make the run fail. An unsupported
26	`--stdin-file-path` is an error because stdin mode requires file-aware behavior.
27	
28	Directory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`,
29	and global Git ignore files. Passing a hidden path explicitly selects it.
30	
31	## JSON-to-YAML projection
32	
33	Formatting preserves the source language and produces output that can replace
34	the input. JSON-to-YAML projection has a different contract: it parses a
35	JSON-family input and emits formatted YAML for inspection or conversion.
36	
37	Use `yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path` to project JSON-family input from stdin
38	to formatted YAML on stdout:
39	
40	```sh
41	yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json < data.json
42	```
43	
44	The command does not read or write the path. It uses the extension to select
45	one exact input grammar:
46	
47	| Extension | Accepted input |
48	| --- | --- |
49	| `.json` | Strict JSON. |
50	| `.jsonc` | JSON with line comments, block comments, and trailing commas. Other JSON5 syntax is rejected. |
51	| `.json5` | JSON5 strings, identifiers, numbers, comments, and trailing commas. |
52	| `.jsonl` and `.ndjson` | One strict JSON value per physical line. Blank records are rejected. |
53	
54	Object member order and duplicate names are preserved. JSON and JSONC keep the
55	source spelling of numbers. JSON5 spellings that YAML would interpret
56	differently are normalized, including `0X` hexadecimal prefixes, leading or
57	trailing decimal points, unary plus, `Infinity`, and `NaN`. Negative
58	hexadecimal integers are emitted in decimal because YAML would otherwise treat
59	them as strings.
60	
61	JSONC and JSON5 comments become YAML comments. JSONL and NDJSON output a YAML
62	document-start marker before every record. A record may be an object, array, or
63	scalar; this does not change how ordinary YAML such as `1\n2` is interpreted by
64	`yamark format`.
65	
66	String escapes are decoded before YAML emission. Lone UTF-16 surrogate escapes
67	are rejected because they do not represent Unicode scalar values. All
68	JSON-family inputs reject nesting deeper than 256 levels. JSON5 also rejects
69	legacy numeric escapes such as `\1`, invalid escaped identifier characters, and
70	U+0085 as whitespace. Characters that YAML cannot carry inside a comment are
71	shown as visible hexadecimal escapes.
72	
73	Projection does not scan JSON strings or comments for embedded Markdown or
74	formatter directives, and it does not dispatch to Prettier or another embedded
75	formatter.
76	
77	`yamark format` continues to skip JSON-family paths and never rewrites them.
78	`Yamark: View JSON as YAML` in VS Code and Positron uses the same JSON-to-YAML
79	projection.
80	
81	## Markdown
82	
83	| Construct | Result | Details |
84	| --- | --- | --- |
85	| Paragraphs | Formats | Wraps by column, paragraph, sentence, or not at all, according to the active Markdown settings. |
86	| ATX headings | Formats | Normalizes spacing. Preserves and, when safe, compacts heading attributes. |
87	| Lists and task lists | Formats | Reflows list paragraphs with container indentation accounted for. Preserves GFM task markers. |
88	| Blockquotes | Formats when supported | Wraps supported blockquote shapes recursively. |
89	| Footnote blocks | Formats or preserves | Wraps definitions by default. A preserve setting keeps definitions byte-for-byte. |
90	| Reference links | Formats around | Treats reference-style links as atomic wrapping tokens. Preserves reference definitions without relocation. |
91	| Inline code and math | Preserves contents; formats around | Recognized spans retain authored whitespace and line endings while surrounding prose formats. |
92	| Nested image links | Formats when safe | Normalizes and wraps simple nested image labels and long destinations. |
93	| Pandoc citations | Formats around | Protects citation spans such as `[@key]` and `[-@key]` while wrapping. |
94	| Quarto divs | Formats when supported | Formats supported fenced div bodies recursively. |
95	| YAML fences | Formats | Formats fenced `yaml` and `yml` blocks as YAML unless locally skipped. |
96	| Markdown fences | Formats | Formats fenced `markdown` and `md` blocks recursively. |
97	| Source fences | Delegates | Can run embedded formatters for Python, R, JSON, GraphQL, CSS, HTML, JavaScript, TypeScript, and related aliases. |
98	| Long Quarto fence openings | Formats when safe | Promotes simple comma-separated options such as `echo=FALSE` to `#| echo: false` lines for a supported fence when wrapping is not `none` and the opening exceeds the configured column, or 72 in `paragraph` and `sentence` modes. For a delegated language, the embedded formatter must succeed; a missing, failed, or disabled formatter preserves the original opening. |
99	| Quarto source fences with `#| fmt: skip` | Preserves | Leaves the fenced chunk unchanged when the directive appears anywhere in the initial consecutive `#|` option block. |
100	| Document Markdown options | Reads | Applies `editor_options.markdown.{wrap,canonical,footnotes,table-widths}` to the body and nested Markdown that follows. |
101	| GFM pipe tables | Formats | Fits supported tables by display width while retaining alignment. `table-widths=preserve` retains separator lengths and source row widths. Git clean/smudge filters otherwise use compact pipe-table output. |
102	| Pandoc tables | Formats when supported | Fits supported simple, grid, and multiline tables to their contents while preserving column alignment and multiline cell breaks. `table-widths=preserve` retains source widths. |
103	| Definition lists | Formats when supported | Normalizes marker spacing and wraps definitions. |
104	| Display math | Preserves | Keeps own-line `$$` display math blocks byte-for-byte. |
105	| Standalone Hugo shortcodes | Preserves tokens; formats between | Complete `{{< ... >}}` and `{{% ... %}}` tokens retain their bytes, including multiline tokens and quoted arguments. Markdown between tokens formats normally. |
106	| Raw HTML, TeX, table captions, and line blocks | Preserves | Leaves the construct unchanged when Yamark does not have a safe rewrite. |
107	| Template spans | Preserves contents; reflows prose | Complete single-line expressions using default or configured delimiters are opaque words in paragraphs and supported prose containers. See [template configuration](reference-config.qmd#template). |
108	
109	For Quarto header promotion, a supported fence is a YAML or Markdown fence, a
110	language with a built-in or configured formatter, or one of the opaque
111	languages Yamark preserves safely: `bash`, `sh`, `shell`, `zsh`, `ojs`, `text`,
112	`console`, `rust`, `toml`, `lua`, `mermaid`, `ini`, `julia`, `sql`, `java`, `c`,
113	`tex`, `latex`, `output`, `powershell`, and `cmd`.
114	
115	## YAML
116	
117	| Construct | Result | Details |
118	| --- | --- | --- |
119	| Block mappings and sequences | Formats | Normalizes indentation and spacing. Does not reorder keys. |
120	| Flow mappings and sequences | Formats | Normalizes spacing. Expands multiline or over-width collections to block style when safe. |
121	| Compact collections | Formats when enabled | Collapses eligible block collections to flow style with `--compact`, `[format].compact`, or `fmt: compact`. |
122	| Scalar folding | Formats when safe | Can emit and rewrap folded prose scalars at the active prose width, including prose already split across plain or quoted continuation lines. Preserves decoded whitespace and comments. |
123	| Literal scalars | Preserves by default | Changes a literal scalar only when it is explicitly marked as Markdown or an embedded formatter target. |
124	| Quoted scalars with hard newlines | Formats when safe | Can emit literal block style when the YAML value stays unchanged. |
125	| Scalars below a mapping key or sequence marker | Formats when safe | Retains the complete entry when preserving a value. Ordinary scalar entries with parent tags, anchors, or comments retain their layout; editable siblings still format. |
126	| Unsafe plain scalars | Quotes | Quotes scalars whose meaning would change in block or flow context. |
127	| Core booleans and nulls | Formats | Normalizes plain values to YAML 1.2 spellings such as `true`, `false`, and `null`. Normalizes explicit core tags when safe. |
128	| Tags and anchors | Preserves | Preserves custom tags, anchors, aliases, and tag/anchor order. May remove a redundant core collection tag when syntax already implies the type. |
129	| Comments and directives | Preserves and reads | Preserves comments around supported nodes. Reads `fmt:` comments as local controls. |
130	| Duplicate keys | Formats around | Does not validate or reorder duplicate keys. May format their values. |
131	| UTF-8 BOM and line endings | Preserves | Preserves a UTF-8 BOM and the dominant CRLF or CR line ending. Rejects UTF-16 BOM input. |
132	| Tab indentation | Preserves or rejects | Preserves tab-indented YAML when no active target requires interpreting it. Rejects targeted formatting that would need to parse the unsupported indentation. |
133	
134	Ordinary scalars remain plain or quoted when conversion to block style would absorb a following indented comment into the value, including across blank lines. Explicit Markdown targets still format; their block content uses deeper indentation when needed to keep the following comment outside the value.
135	
136	### JSON Lines (JSONL) as YAML streams
137	
138	Path-aware formatting recognizes a `.yaml` or `.yml` stream made of two or more
139	unmarked, one-line YAML flow-mapping roots, one per physical line with no
140	separate trivia lines. It inserts the `---` document-start marker before every
141	record, including the first.
142	
143	JSON objects are the common case, but the trigger is based on YAML shape and is
144	not restricted to strict JSON objects.
145	
146	Normal `--line-width` rules still determine whether each record and its nested
147	collections stay in flow style or expand to block style. A single flow-mapping
148	root or a stream containing any non-flow-mapping root follows the normal YAML
149	path instead.
150	
151	See the generated [JSON Lines example](examples.qmd#json-lines-as-a-yaml-stream).
152	
153	## Python and R source files
154	
155	| Construct | Result | Details |
156	| --- | --- | --- |
157	| Consecutive own-line `#|` comments | Formats | Parses the comment body as YAML and emits it with the original hashpipe prefix. |
158	| Marked Markdown comments and strings | Formats | Formats supported own-line comment blocks and supported multiline string literals, accounting for their prefix or indentation. |
159	| Marked external source strings | Delegates | Sends a supported multiline string literal to the named built-in or configured formatter and re-indents the result. |
160	| Surrounding Python or R | Preserves | Does not format source outside recognized or explicitly marked targets. |
161	
162	Every non-empty line in a comment target must use the same comment prefix;
163	empty comment lines may omit its trailing space. Python string targets use
164	triple quotes with no prefix, or an `r`, `f`, `rf`, or `fr` prefix; the closing
165	delimiter must be on a later line. R targets use a multiline standard or raw
166	string. Markdown formatting rejects backslashes in non-raw Python and R strings
167	because rewriting them could change the host-language value.
168	
169	The generated [hashpipe YAML example](examples.qmd#hashpipe-yaml-in-source-files)
170	shows the automatic source-file transformation.
171	
172	## Embedded formatter dispatch
173	
174	External formatters run only for explicit targets or recognized Markdown fence
175	languages. Built-in aliases include `ruff`, `air`, `mdformat`, and the
176	`prettier` family.
177	
178	| Target name or fence language | Built-in formatter |
179	| --- | --- |
180	| `python`, `ruff` | Ruff |
181	| `r`, `air` | Air |
182	| `mdformat` | mdformat |
183	| `json`, `prettier-json` | Prettier with a `.json` path |
184	| `jsonc`, `prettier-jsonc` | Prettier with a `.jsonc` path |
185	| `json5`, `prettier-json5` | Prettier with a `.json5` path |
186	| `graphql`, `gql`, `graphqls`, `prettier-graphql` | Prettier with a `.graphql` path |
187	| `css`, `prettier-css` | Prettier with a `.css` path |
188	| `scss`, `prettier-scss` | Prettier with a `.scss` path |
189	| `less`, `prettier-less` | Prettier with a `.less` path |
190	| `postcss`, `pcss`, `prettier-postcss` | Prettier with a `.pcss` path |
191	| `html`, `prettier-html` | Prettier with a `.html` path |
192	| `js`, `javascript`, `prettier-js` | Prettier with a `.js` path |
193	| `jsx`, `prettier-jsx` | Prettier with a `.jsx` path |
194	| `ts`, `typescript`, `prettier-ts` | Prettier with a `.ts` path |
195	| `tsx`, `prettier-tsx` | Prettier with a `.tsx` path |
196	
197	Markdown fences named `markdown` or `md` are formatted recursively instead of
198	using mdformat. An [`[embedded.<name>]`](reference-config.qmd#embedded) entry
199	replaces the built-in mapping for that exact name.
200	
201	The default aliases are optional. A configured formatter is also optional when
202	its command's first argv item is exactly `ruff`, `air`, `mdformat`, or
203	`prettier`. A missing executable or nonzero exit preserves the target for
204	either kind. Yamark reports the reason as a note only with `--diagnostics`.
205	
206	A successful process that writes to stderr is an error. Any other configured
207	formatter is strict: a missing executable or nonzero exit is an error. These
208	formatter errors happen before Yamark writes the formatted file. See the
209	[`[embedded]` schema](reference-config.qmd#embedded) and
210	[`--skip-embedded-formatters`](reference-options.qmd#execution-controls).
211	
212	## Layout repair
213	
214	Yamark recognizes two narrow layout cues. Only the unmatched opener is a repair
215	for ill-formed input:
216	
217	- An unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping begins as a mapping
218	  value or sequence item asks Yamark to collapse that one collection to flow
219	  style.
220	- A physical newline inside a complete flow collection is valid multiline YAML.
221	  It asks Yamark to expand that collection to block style. Compact mode
222	  suppresses this multiline intent.
223	
224	The opener may be on the value line or on the following line after an empty
225	mapping value header. Adjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not
226	layout hints.
227	
228	When the requested flow form fits the available `--line-width`, Yamark removes
229	the unmatched opener and emits the collection in flow style. Otherwise it
230	preserves the hinted collection as typed. It does not fail solely because the
231	requested flow form is too wide, and surrounding YAML may still be formatted.
232	The [layout examples](examples.qmd#collapse-to-flow-by-typing-a-bracket) show
233	each accepted gesture before and after formatting.
234	
235	## Failure behavior
236	
237	Yamark is a formatter, not a general validator. It formats supported regions
238	and leaves unsupported regions unchanged when they are not explicitly
239	targeted and it has no safe rewrite.
240	
241	Yamark parses YAML before formatting. For Markdown and Markdown-valued YAML
242	scalars, it emits only transformations supported by its parser. An embedded
243	formatter can change only a recognized fence or an explicitly marked source or
244	YAML target.
245	
246	An explicit directive instead requires a supported target. A missing or
247	unsupported target or an unknown formatter name is an error for that file.
248	Formatter execution follows the optional and strict failure rules above.
249	
250	Input-decoding, parsing, formatting, file-read, and external-formatter errors
251	happen before Yamark writes that file, so these errors leave its original
252	content unchanged. A write error is reported, but writes are direct rather than
253	atomic; Yamark does not promise rollback after a write begins.
254	
255	A multi-file write run is not transactional. Other files can be written even
256	when one input fails.

12	## Markdown settings
13	
14	| Behavior | [Directive](reference-directives.qmd#markdown-targets-and-settings) | [Front matter](#document-markdown-options) | [`yamark.toml`](reference-config.qmd#format) | [Command line](cli-help.qmd#yamark-format) | Default |
15	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
16	| Prose wrapping | `wrap=` | `editor_options.markdown.wrap` | `[format].wrap` | `--wrap` | Column 72 |
17	| Table widths | `table-widths=` | `editor_options.markdown.table-widths` | `[format].table_widths` | `--table-widths` | `fit` |
18	| Canonical spelling | `canonical=` or `canonical` | `editor_options.markdown.canonical` | - | `--canonical` | Off |
19	| Footnote definitions | `footnotes=` | `editor_options.markdown.footnotes` | - | `--preserve-footnotes` | Format |
20	| Horizontal-rule marker | - | - | `[format].markdown_horizontal_rule` | - | `---` |
21	
22	### Wrapping values
23	
24	| Value | Effect |
25	| --- | --- |
26	| `none` | Do not wrap Markdown prose. |
27	| `paragraph` | Put each paragraph on one physical line. |
28	| `sentence` | Put each sentence on its own line without column wrapping. |
29	| `sentence:<n>` | Put each sentence on its own line and wrap long sentences to column `<n>`. |
30	| A positive integer | Wrap prose to that column without forcing sentence boundaries. |
31	
32	`sentence:<n>` is a Yamark-specific extension. RStudio's visual writer does not
33	recognize the combined value.
34	
35	### Table widths
36	
37	`fit` sizes supported pipe, simple, grid, and multiline table columns from
38	their contents, with consistent padding. It can shrink excessive widths or
39	expand cramped columns. Both modes preserve column alignment and multiline
40	cell breaks.
41	
42	`preserve` retains the source widths while still formatting cell contents.
43	For Pandoc tables, this keeps the borders and gaps that determine widths. For
44	pipe tables, it keeps separator lengths and row widths, even when the original
45	rows are not aligned with one another.
46	
47	Pandoc can use source widths to determine rendered column proportions and
48	wrapping. Choose `preserve` when those widths are intentional:
49	
50	```markdown
51	<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->
52	+----------+------------------+
53	| Name     | Description      |
54	+==========+==================+
55	| A        | Short text       |
56	+----------+------------------+
57	```
58	
59	Use `scope=file` for a document-wide choice or `scope=from-here` for subsequent
60	tables. A later `table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths.
61	Without an explicit scope, this option follows the usual Markdown directive
62	default of `scope=file`.
63	
64	The setting also works in front matter, `yamark.toml`, and the command line.
65	Explicit renderer settings such as Quarto's `tbl-colwidths` remain unchanged.
66	`fmt: skip` preserves the entire table when exact source layout matters.
67	Unsupported table structures remain unchanged in either mode.
68	
69	### Canonical and footnote values
70	
71	`canonical` accepts `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0` in front matter
72	and directives. A bare `canonical` directive means `canonical=true`. Canonical
73	mode rewrites supported `_emphasis_` and `__strong__` spans as `*emphasis*` and
74	`**strong**`. It preserves protected or unsupported spans, including intraword
75	underscores, code spans, link destinations, raw HTML, and template content.
76	
77	For `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` format footnote
78	definitions. `preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` preserve them.
79	`--preserve-footnotes` preserves Markdown footnote definitions byte-for-byte.
80	
81	## YAML settings
82	
83	| Behavior | Control | Default | Effect |
84	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
85	| Structural line width | `--line-width <n>` | 80 | Expands block-renderable flow collections when they exceed the width. Over-width flow collections that cannot be rendered safely in block style may be preserved. Also bounds compact and layout-repair output. |
86	| Folded scalar prose width | `--prose-width <n>` | 72 | Wraps eligible folded YAML prose. |
87	| Block indentation | `--indent-width <n>` | 2 | Sets indentation for emitted block mappings and sequences. |
88	| Compact collections | `--compact`, `[format].compact`, or `fmt: compact` | Off | Collapses eligible block collections to flow style when they fit. |
89	| Aligned flow mappings | `fmt: table` or `fmt: compact table` | Off | Aligns a following sequence of compatible flow mappings. The compact form first collapses eligible block rows. |
90	
91	All width and indentation values must be positive integers.
92	
93	Canonical mode also permits limited rewrapping of short existing folded YAML
94	prose scalars when their value stays unchanged.
95	
96	## Execution controls
97	
98	| Control | Effect |
99	| --- | --- |
100	| `--diagnostics` | For YAML input, emits trace counters; it also emits notes for skipped or failing optional embedded formatters. |
101	| `--skip-embedded-formatters` | Disables external formatters while keeping Yamark's Markdown, YAML, front matter, and recursive Markdown formatting active. |
102	| `--config <path>` | Uses one explicit `yamark.toml` for all selected files instead of discovering one per file. |
103	
104	### Embedded formatter controls
105	
106	| Need | Control |
107	| --- | --- |
108	| Select a target | Use a recognized Markdown fence language or a [`fmt: <name>` directive](reference-directives.qmd#templates-and-embedded-formatters). |
109	| Register or replace a formatter | Add an [`[embedded.<name>]` table](reference-config.qmd#embedded) to `yamark.toml`. |
110	| Disable external formatters for one run | Pass `--skip-embedded-formatters`. |
111	| Explain an optional formatter skip | Pass `--diagnostics`. |
112	
113	Write, check, diff, and stdin behavior is documented under
114	[Command line](cli-help.qmd#modes-output-and-status).
115	
116	## Document Markdown options
117	
118	Markdown front matter can set document-local options under
119	`editor_options.markdown`:
120	
121	```markdown
122	---
123	editor_options:
124	  markdown:
125	    wrap: sentence:72
126	    canonical: true
127	    footnotes: preserve
128	    table-widths: preserve
129	---
130	This is __strong__. This is _emphasis_.
131	```
132	
133	| Key | Accepted values |
134	| --- | --- |
135	| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer column. |
136	| `table-widths` | `fit` or `preserve`. |
137	| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |
138	| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |
139	
140	Unknown front-matter keys and unrecognized values are ignored; the
141	corresponding base setting remains active. Invalid `yamark.toml` keys or
142	directive values are errors instead.
143	
144	These options apply after the front matter to the Markdown body, recursive
145	`markdown` or `md` fences, and Markdown-valued YAML scalars in nested YAML
146	regions.
147	
148	Yamark also reads `editor.markdown` for compatibility, but only when
149	`editor_options.markdown` is absent. It does not merge the two tables. Git
150	filter subcommands use their own wrapping options and do not read document
151	options.
152	
153	## Interaction rules
154	
155	Markdown settings are applied in this order:
156	
157	1. Command defaults and config establish the base settings. Explicit `--wrap`
158	   and `--table-widths` values override their corresponding `[format]` config
159	   values.
160	2. Document front matter overrides the corresponding base Markdown settings
161	   for the document body and its nested Markdown regions.
162	3. Directives then override the corresponding settings within their scope.
163	4. `--preserve-footnotes` is the final exception: it preserves footnote
164	   definitions even when front matter or a directive requests formatting.
165	
166	Other interactions:
167	
168	- `--compact` enables compact mode even if `[format].compact` is `false`. A
169	  scoped `fmt: compact=false` directive can disable it for its target, region,
170	  or file.
171	- `editor_options.markdown` takes the place of the compatibility
172	  `editor.markdown` table when both are present; the tables are not merged.
173	- Git filter clean and smudge commands use their own Markdown wrapping options.
174	  They do not read document Markdown options.

56	### Markdown in YAML {#markdown-valued-yaml-scalars}
57	
58	Yamark can format Markdown stored in YAML in three ways: tag the value with
59	`!markdown`, use `!md` as a shorter alias, or put `# fmt: markdown` on the line
60	before the value. The example below shows the full tag and comment forms.
61	
62	A `prompts.yaml` or `agents.yaml` file can use any of these forms. Yamark wraps
63	the selected value as Markdown, choosing folded or literal block style from the
64	content.
65	
66	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
67	**Before**
68	
69	```yaml
70	agents:
71	  reviewer:
72	    instructions: !markdown "Focus on correctness and tests. Flag any change that lacks a regression test. Prefer concrete suggestions: name the function, name the case."
73	  summarizer:
74	    # fmt: markdown
75	    instructions: |
76	      You write release notes.
77	
78	      - One bullet per user-visible change.
79	      - No internal refactors.
80	```
81	
82	**After**
83	
84	```yaml
85	agents:
86	  reviewer:
87	    instructions: !markdown |
88	      Focus on correctness and tests. Flag any change that lacks a regression
89	      test. Prefer concrete suggestions: name the function, name the case.
90	  summarizer:
91	    # fmt: markdown
92	    instructions: |
93	      You write release notes.
94	
95	      - One bullet per user-visible change.
96	      - No internal refactors.
97	```
98	::::
99	
100	The tagged value contains only prose, so Yamark rewraps it as a folded block.
101	The comment-marked value contains a list, so Yamark keeps literal block style
102	(`|`) because folding would destroy the line breaks Markdown depends on.
103	
104	### Source code in YAML
105	
106	YAML values can also contain source code. Use `# fmt: python`, `# fmt: r`, or
107	the name of another configured formatter before a literal block. When the
108	formatter is available, Yamark formats the block and restores its indentation
109	in the YAML file.
110	
111	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
112	**Before**
113	
114	```yaml
115	# fmt: python
116	preflight: |
117	  def check(items):return all(x>0 for x in items)
118	```
119	
120	**After**
121	
122	```yaml
123	# fmt: python
124	preflight: |
125	  def check(items):
126	    return all(x > 0 for x in items)
127	```
128	::::

130	### YAML scalar presentation
131	
132	Yamark changes scalar spelling only when the parsed YAML value and tag
133	stay equivalent. It can simplify safe quoted strings, keep strings that
134	would be misread as booleans, convert hard newlines to literal blocks,
135	and fold long prose strings.
136	
137	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
138	**Before**
139	
140	```yaml
141	title: "hello"
142	boolish: "true"
143	body: "alpha\nbeta\n"
144	summary: "This package formats YAML front matter and configuration files while preserving semantics, comments, and repository-friendly diffs."
145	```
146	
147	**After**
148	
149	```yaml
150	title: hello
151	boolish: "true"
152	body: |
153	  alpha
154	  beta
155	summary: >-
156	  This package formats YAML front matter and configuration files while
157	  preserving semantics, comments, and repository-friendly diffs.
158	```

356	## YAML layout
357	
358	### JSON Lines as a YAML stream
359	
360	Give a JSON Lines file containing two or more object records a `.yaml` or
361	`.yml` extension, with one record per line, then format it normally. Yamark
362	inserts a leading `---` document-start marker before every record, including
363	the first, producing a valid YAML multi-document stream. The example below uses
364	records from agent runs.
365	
366	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
367	**Before**
368	
369	```yaml
370	{"id":1,"profile":{"name":"planner","active":true}}
371	{"id":2,"profile":{"name":"researcher","active":true},"usage":{"input_tokens":640,"output_tokens":128}}
372	{"id":3,"profile":{"name":"reviewer","active":true,"model":"gpt-5","region":"us","tools":["search","python"]},"events":[{"type":"tool_call","tools":["search","open","python","write"]},{"type":"usage","tokens":{"input":900,"output":240}},{"type":"completion","status":"ok"}]}
373	```
374	
375	**After**
376	
377	```yaml
378	---
379	{id: 1, profile: {name: planner, active: true}}
380	---
381	id: 2
382	profile: {name: researcher, active: true}
383	usage: {input_tokens: 640, output_tokens: 128}
384	---
385	id: 3
386	profile:
387	  name: reviewer
388	  active: true
389	  model: gpt-5
390	  region: us
391	  tools: [search, python]
392	events:
393	  - {type: tool_call, tools: [search, open, python, write]}
394	  - {type: usage, tokens: {input: 900, output: 240}}
395	  - {type: completion, status: ok}
396	```
397	::::
398	
399	Yamark keeps each document as compact as the width allows. The first record
400	stays in flow style; the second expands only its root mapping; the third also
401	expands `profile` and `events`. Smaller mappings and sequences remain in flow
402	style whenever they still fit within `--line-width`. This conversion is for
403	object records, not arbitrary JSON values.
404	
405	### Aligned flow-mapping tables
406	
407	A sequence of similar flow mappings can be easier to scan as a table. Mark it
408	with `# fmt: table` and Yamark aligns columns by key:
409	
410	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
411	**Before**
412	
413	```yaml
414	# fmt: table
415	- {name: alpha,type: string,default: [one,two],description: "Short"}
416	- {name: beta,type: int,default: 0,description: "Number"}
417	```
418	
419	**After**
420	
421	```yaml
422	# fmt: table
423	- {name: alpha, type: string, default: [one, two], description: Short}
424	- {name: beta,  type: int,    default: 0,          description: Number}
425	```
426	::::
427	
428	### Compact collections
429	
430	Short, simple block collections can read better as a single flow line.
431	Enable `compact = true` in `yamark.toml` (or pass `--compact`) and
432	Yamark collapses eligible block mappings and sequences that fit the
433	structural width:
434	
435	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
436	**Before**
437	
438	```yaml
439	tags:
440	  - yaml
441	  - markdown
442	  - docs
443	package:
444	  name: yamark
445	  language: rust
446	```
447	
448	**After**
449	
450	```yaml
451	tags: [yaml, markdown, docs]
452	package: {name: yamark, language: rust}
453	```
454	::::
455	
456	Collections with comments, aliases, tags, anchors, multiline scalars, or
457	block scalars stay in block style.
458	
459	### Collapse to flow by typing a bracket
460	
461	Drop an unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping value starts and
462	Yamark reads it as a layout hint: collapse this collection onto one line. The
463	file doesn't parse as you typed it, but the intent is obvious - Yamark removes
464	the opener and emits flow style.
465	
466	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
467	**Before**
468	
469	```yaml
470	tags: [
471	  - yaml
472	  - markdown
473	  - docs
474	```
475	
476	**After**
477	
478	```yaml
479	tags: [yaml, markdown, docs]
480	```
481	::::
482	
483	The opener may also be detached onto the next line after an empty mapping value
484	header:
485	
486	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
487	**Before**
488	
489	```yaml
490	tags:
491	[
492	  - yaml
493	  - markdown
494	  - docs
495	```
496	
497	**After**
498	
499	```yaml
500	tags: [yaml, markdown, docs]
501	```
502	::::
503	
504	Adjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not repaired as layout hints.
505	
506	A newline inside an existing flow collection requests the reverse change: expand
507	the collection to block style.
508	
509	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
510	**Before**
511	
512	```yaml
513	- {a: b,
514	   c: d}
515	```
516	
517	**After**
518	
519	```yaml
520	- a: b
521	  c: d
522	```
523	::::
524	
525	See [Supported files and syntax -> Layout repair](reference-files.qmd#layout-repair)
526	for the acceptance rules.

528	## Fenced and nested content
529	
530	### Recursive Markdown code fences
531	
532	YAML fences are formatted as YAML. Markdown fences are formatted
533	recursively, so nested YAML inside nested Markdown is formatted too.
534	
535	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
536	**Before**
537	
538	`````markdown
539	```yaml
540	# fmt: table
541	- {name: a,type: int,default: 0}
542	- {name: long_name,type: string,default: ""}
543	```
544	
545	````markdown
546	#   Inner
547	
548	```yaml
549	items: [a,b]
550	```
551	````
552	`````
553	
554	**After**
555	
556	`````markdown
557	```yaml
558	# fmt: table
559	- {name: a,         type: int,    default: 0}
560	- {name: long_name, type: string, default: ""}
561	```
562	
563	````markdown
564	# Inner
565	
566	```yaml
567	items: [a, b]
568	```
569	````
570	`````
571	::::
572	
573	### Prettier-backed web and data fences
574	
575	When `prettier` is on `PATH`, JSON, JSONC, JSON5, GraphQL, CSS, SCSS, Less,
576	PostCSS, HTML, JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, and TSX fenced blocks are handed to
577	it. Python and R fences go to Ruff and Air the same way:
578	
579	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
580	**Before**
581	
582	````markdown
583	```json
584	{"name":"yamark","tags":["yaml","markdown","formatter"],"engines":{"node":">=18"}}
585	```
586	
587	```ts
588	function format(input:string):string{return input.trim()}
589	```
590	````
591	
592	**After**
593	
594	````markdown
595	```json
596	{
597	  "name": "yamark",
598	  "tags": ["yaml", "markdown", "formatter"],
599	  "engines": { "node": ">=18" }
600	}
601	```
602	
603	```ts
604	function format(input: string): string {
605	  return input.trim();
606	}
607	```
608	````
609	::::
610	
611	A missing `prettier` leaves the fence unchanged. Override or disable a
612	language with `[embedded.<language>]` in `yamark.toml`, or skip them all with
613	`--skip-embedded-formatters`.

1	# Yamark
2	
3	Yamark is a fast formatter for YAML and Markdown. It formats whole files and embedded content, keeping source readable and changes easy to review. Regions without a supported rewrite stay unchanged.
4	
5	For supported embedded code, Yamark can also call Ruff, Air, Prettier, or another configured formatter.
6	
7	See the [documentation](https://t-kalinowski.github.io/yamark/) for examples, configuration, editor integrations, and the full syntax reference.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed, run Yamark directly from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/yamark/) without a separate install:
12	
13	```sh
14	uvx yamark format config.yaml docs/
15	```
16	
17	This formats the selected files in place. To install a persistent `yamark` command:
18	
19	```sh
20	uv tool install yamark
21	```
22	
23	## Usage
24	
25	The examples below use an installed `yamark` command. To keep running from PyPI without installing it, replace `yamark` with `uvx yamark`.
26	
27	Format one or more files or directories in place:
28	
29	```sh
30	yamark format config.yaml docs/
31	```
32	
33	Format the current directory:
34	
35	```sh
36	yamark format
37	```
38	
39	Check whether files are already formatted without writing changes:
40	
41	```sh
42	yamark format --check docs/
43	```
44	
45	Show a unified diff without writing changes:
46	
47	```sh
48	yamark format --diff docs/
49	```
50	
51	Format stdin for editor and CI integrations:
52	
53	```sh
54	yamark format --stdin-file-path config.yaml < config.yaml
55	```
56	
57	Convert JSON-family input from stdin to formatted YAML on stdout:
58	
59	```sh
60	yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json5 < data.json5
61	```
62	
63	The path is not read or written. Its suffix selects the exact JSON dialect. This is a conversion, not source formatting.
64	
65	Directory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and global Git ignore files by default. Pass a hidden path explicitly to format it.
66	
67	While formatting is enabled, standalone `{{< ... >}}` and `{{% ... %}}` shortcode tokens are preserved, including multiline tokens and quoted arguments. Directive-looking text inside a recognized token is data. Yamark does not match shortcode names or interpret their bodies: Markdown between tokens formats normally. An unterminated token or quote preserves the rest of the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This does not guarantee rendering equivalence for arbitrary Hugo or Jinja templates.
68	
69	To disable body formatting, surround the region with `<!-- fmt: off -->` and `<!-- fmt: on -->`. While formatting is disabled, directives follow the existing linewise policy: a recognized `fmt: on` line resumes formatting even if the surrounding text resembles a shortcode argument, code fence, HTML, or math block.
70	
71	Explicitly skipped Markdown retains its bytes, including trailing spaces and line endings: `<!-- fmt: skip -->` preserves the next selected node, `<!-- fmt: off -->` preserves the disabled region, and `<!-- fmt: skip file -->` preserves the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This protection survives supported nesting in Markdown fences and divs; surrounding Markdown still formats.
72

74	
75	The VS Code and Positron formatter extension lives in `editors/vscode/`. See the [editor guide][editor-docs] for installation and configuration.

2	# fmt: skip file
3	title: Directives
4	description: Tell Yamark what to format, skip, preserve, or configure from inside the file.
5	---
6	
7	<!-- fmt: skip file -->
8	
9	The source file is the primary interface. Put a small `fmt:` directive next to
10	the text it controls, then let an editor or repository integration run Yamark.
11	Because directives are comments, the formatting choice stays with the text.
12	The comment marker depends on the file:
13	
14	| File | Directive comment |
15	| --- | --- |
16	| Markdown and Quarto | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` |
17	| YAML, Python, and R | `# fmt: ...` |
18	
19	Quarto chunk options use `#|`; for example, `#| fmt: skip`.
20	
21	## Target the next value or block
22	
23	Most directives apply to the next supported target. In a YAML file, that target
24	is usually a scalar node. In a Python or R file, it is usually a string literal
25	or a contiguous source-comment block. The directive does not format the
26	surrounding Python or R source code.
27	
28	## YAML files
29	
30	Mark a scalar as Markdown and choose sentence wrapping for that scalar:
31	
32	```yaml
33	# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
34	description: "Explain the project in a few clear sentences."
35	other_value: "This is ordinary YAML, not Markdown."
36	```
37	
38	The directive attaches to `description`, the next scalar. A tagged scalar is
39	another way to mark Markdown when the setting should travel with the value:
40	
41	```yaml
42	instructions: !markdown |
43	  # Review
44	
45	  Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues.
46	```
47	
48	Use the same placement for an embedded formatter. The formatter name is the
49	language after `fmt:`:
50	
51	```yaml
52	# fmt: python
53	script: |
54	  def check(items):return all(item > 0 for item in items)
55	```
56	
57	YAML also supports directives on a collection parent when the setting describes
58	the collection rather than a scalar:
59	
60	```yaml
61	# fmt: table
62	- {name: alpha, type: string, default: ""}
63	- {name: beta, type: integer, default: 0}
64	```
65	
66	## Python files
67	
68	Put `# fmt: markdown` immediately before the string literal or comment block
69	that contains Markdown:
70	
71	```python
72	# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
73	REVIEW_PROMPT = """
74	# Review
75	
76	Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues. Prefer specific examples.
77	"""
78	```
79	
80	The `#` lines inside the string are Markdown content. Python outside the
81	marked target is left for a Python formatter such as Ruff.
82	
83	The same directive can target a Markdown comment block:
84	
85	```python
86	# fmt: markdown
87	# # Filters
88	#
89	# Apply the most specific filter first.
90	#
91	# - Each filter is a single expression.
92	```
93	
94	For a non-Markdown embedded language, use its formatter name:
95	
96	```python
97	# fmt: r
98	analysis = """
99	f <- function(x) x + 1
100	"""
101	```
102	
103	## R files
104	
105	R uses the same `# fmt:` marker. It can target a raw string literal used for a
106	vignette, help text, or a Shiny message:
107	
108	```r
109	# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
110	help_text <- r"(
111	# Filters
112	
113	Apply the most specific filter first. Explain why a filter matched.
114	)"
115	```
116	
117	It can also target a contiguous Markdown comment block:
118	
119	```r
120	# fmt: markdown
121	# # Filters
122	#
123	# Apply the most specific filter first.
124	#
125	# - Each filter is a single expression.
126	```
127	
128	For source code inside a YAML literal scalar, use the language formatter name
129	in the same way as in a YAML file:
130	
131	```yaml
132	# fmt: r
133	analysis: |
134	  f <- function(x)x+1
135	```
136	
137	## Control a region or a whole file
138	
139	The scope is part of the directive. `next` is the default for target directives.
140	Use `from-here` for the rest of a region, and `file` for a document-wide
141	setting:
142	
143	| Scope | Applies to |
144	| --- | --- |
145	| `scope=next` | The next supported string, scalar, collection, or comment block. |
146	| `scope=from-here` | Supported content from this point until another directive changes the setting. |
147	| `scope=file` | The whole file, including supported content before the directive. |
148	
149	Skip one target:
150	
151	```yaml
152	normal: [1, 2, 3]
153	# fmt: skip
154	manual:
155	    -   [ 1,2,3]
156	```
157	
158	Preserve a region and resume formatting afterward:
159	
160	```markdown
161	<!-- fmt: off -->
162	#   Keep this heading ##
163	
164	<!-- fmt: on -->
165	```
166	
167	Skip a whole file by putting the file directive at the top. YAML, Python, and R
168	use the same hash-comment form:
169	
170	```text
171	# fmt: skip file
172	```
173	
174	Markdown uses an HTML comment:
175	
176	```markdown
177	<!-- fmt: skip file -->
178	```
179	
180	A whole-file skip is useful for generated files or files whose layout is
181	intentionally outside Yamark's scope.
182	
183	Markdown skip controls retain trailing spaces and line endings in the selected
184	content, including supported nested Markdown.
185	
186	## Preserve intentional table widths
187	
188	Yamark normally fits table columns to their contents. Keep a table's authored
189	widths while still formatting its contents:
190	
191	```markdown
192	<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->
193	+----------+------------------+
194	| Name     | Description      |
195	+==========+==================+
196	| A        | Short text       |
197	+----------+------------------+
198	```
199	
200	Use `scope=file` to preserve widths throughout the document, or
201	`scope=from-here` for subsequent tables. A later
202	`table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths. Both modes retain
203	column alignment. Fitting widths can change the rendered proportions of
204	Pandoc tables; preserving widths can retain excessive or cramped padding.
205	
206	For Markdown inside YAML, Python, or R, the same option can accompany the
207	target marker: `# fmt: markdown table-widths=preserve`.
208	
209	## Set file-specific Markdown options
210	
211	Use `scope=file` when the file should have a different Markdown policy from the
212	repository default:
213	
214	```markdown
215	<!-- fmt: wrap=sentence:72 scope=file -->
216	```
217	
218	This puts one sentence per line and wraps long sentences at column 72. Other
219	file-wide Markdown options include `canonical=true` and
220	`footnotes=preserve`:
221	
222	```markdown
223	<!-- fmt: canonical=true footnotes=preserve scope=file -->
224	```
225	
226	For a YAML file or a hashpipe YAML stream in Python or R, use the same scope to
227	set YAML behavior for the whole file:
228	
229	```yaml
230	# fmt: compact=false scope=file
231	```
232	
233	An option-only directive such as `# fmt: canonical=true` adjusts the next
234	already-marked Markdown scalar. It does not turn an ordinary YAML scalar into a
235	Markdown target:
236	
237	```yaml
238	# fmt: canonical=true
239	first: !markdown "This is __strong__ Markdown."
240	second: "This is ordinary YAML text."
241	```
242	
243	## Arrange for Yamark to run automatically
244	
245	Once directives are in the files, configure Yamark to run as part of the
246	workflow:
247	
248	- In an editor, enable format on save. The [Editors](editors.qmd) page shows
249	  the VS Code and Positron settings. This is the most direct way to see a
250	  directive take effect while editing.
251	- In a pre-commit hook, run `yamark format`. In CI, use
252	  `yamark format --check` to verify files without changing them.
253	
254	The experimental [Git Filter](git-filter.qmd) serves a narrower workflow: it
255	stores selected Markdown files sentence-per-line while keeping the working tree
256	column-wrapped.
257	
258	## When a repository default is better
259	
260	Use `yamark.toml` for settings that should apply broadly rather than to one
261	piece of text. Keep local exceptions in directives so they stay beside the
262	content they explain.
263	
264	For example, a repository can choose sentence-per-line Markdown and compact
265	YAML collections by default:
266	
267	```toml
268	[format]
269	wrap = "sentence:88"
270	compact = true
271	```
272	
273	Yamark discovers `yamark.toml` from each formatted file's directory upward.
274	Use the [Configuration reference](reference-config.qmd) for the full
275	`[format]`, `[template]`, `[embedded]`, and `[paths]` schema.
276	
277	## For one-off runs
278	
279	Command-line options are useful for trying a policy, checking files in CI, or
280	overriding a repository default for one invocation:
281	
282	```sh
283	yamark format --wrap sentence:72 docs/
284	yamark format --compact config.yaml
285	yamark format --check docs/
286	```

288	Use the [Directive syntax reference](reference-directives.qmd) for every
289	accepted form, scope, and value.

3	title: Directive syntax
4	description: Exact fmt comment forms, targets, scopes, values, and effects.
5	---
6	
7	<!-- fmt: skip file -->
8	
9	Directives are comments whose trimmed content starts with `fmt:`. This page is
10	an exact syntax lookup. For a guided path through YAML, Python, and R examples,
11	see [Directives](directives.qmd).
12	
13	## Comment forms
14	
15	| Host | Form | Placement |
16	| --- | --- | --- |
17	| Markdown | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` | An own-line HTML comment. |
18	| YAML | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment. `fmt: table` and `fmt: compact table` may also be same-line comments on an empty-valued collection parent; a populated parent is an error. |
19	| Python and R | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment before a supported comment or string target. |
20	
21	## Scopes
22	
23	| Scope | Meaning |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| `scope=next` | Apply to the next supported target. This is the default for target-selecting, compact, table, and embedded-formatter directives. |
26	| `scope=from-here` | Apply from the directive until another directive changes the same state. |
27	| `scope=file` | Apply throughout the current parsed document or nested region, including supported nodes before the directive. At the top level, that region is the physical file. |
28	
29	Not every directive accepts every scope. The tables below list the supported
30	forms. An unsupported or misspelled explicit scope is an error. Template
31	delimiter directives use the contextual rule described below instead of one
32	fixed default.
33	
34	Scopes stop at the current parsed document or nested-region boundary. A
35	directive inside a recursive fence affects that fence, not its Markdown host or
36	sibling fences. A `scope=file` directive inside one hashpipe YAML block does not
37	span later blocks. `fmt: skip file` in Markdown front matter is the exception:
38	it preserves the outer Markdown document.
39	
40	## Preserve content
41	
42	| Directive | Scope | Effect |
43	| --- | --- | --- |
44	| `fmt: skip` | Next | Preserve the next supported target. `fmt: skip scope=next` is equivalent. |
45	| `fmt: skip file` | File | Preserve the current parsed document or nested region. `fmt: skip scope=file` is equivalent. |
46	| `fmt: off` | From here | Preserve content until `fmt: on`, or through the end of Markdown and source regions. `fmt: off scope=from-here` is equivalent. |
47	| `fmt: on` | - | Resume formatting after `fmt: off`. It does not accept an explicit scope. |
48	
49	The same control uses the host's comment form:
50	
51	```yaml
52	# fmt: skip
53	manual: [[ 1,2,3], [4,5,6]]
54	```
55	
56	```markdown
57	<!-- fmt: off -->
58	*   keep
59	    this
60	    list
61	<!-- fmt: on -->
62	```
63	
64	Preserve-control lifecycle checks are host-specific. YAML rejects a targetless
65	`skip`, a stray `on`, a nested `off`, and an `off` without a later `on`.
66	Markdown and source regions allow `skip` at the end and let `off` preserve
67	through the end of the region.
68	
69	## Markdown targets and settings
70	
71	| Form | Default scope | Effect |
72	| --- | --- | --- |
73	| `fmt: markdown` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown: a Markdown block, including a supported fence; a YAML scalar; or a source string or comment block. |
74	| `fmt: markdown wrap=sentence canonical=true` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown and set its options. |
75	| `fmt: wrap=sentence` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Change wrapping for an already recognized Markdown region without marking unrelated content. |
76	| `fmt: table-widths=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve widths in supported Markdown tables while formatting contents. Use `scope=next` immediately before one table. |
77	| `fmt: canonical` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Enable canonical Markdown spelling. `canonical=true` is equivalent. |
78	| `fmt: footnotes=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve footnote definitions in the affected Markdown. |
79	
80	Option-only YAML directives tune the next scalar only if it is already marked
81	as Markdown:
82	
83	```yaml
84	# fmt: canonical=true
85	first: !markdown "This is __strong__."
86	second: "This is __not__ Markdown."
87	```
88	
89	For `scope=from-here` or `scope=file`, `fmt: markdown` must include at least one
90	actual Markdown option. A broad-scope directive changes Markdown settings; it
91	does not turn every plain scalar into Markdown.
92	
93	Accepted option values:
94	
95	| Option | Values |
96	| --- | --- |
97	| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer. |

105	## YAML collections
106	
107	| Directive | Scope | Effect |
108	| --- | --- | --- |
109	| `fmt: compact` | Next | Enable block-to-flow compaction for the next eligible collection. |
110	| `fmt: compact false` | Next | Disable compaction for the next eligible collection. `fmt: compact=false` is equivalent. |
111	| `fmt: compact scope=from-here` | From here | Enable compaction until another compact directive changes the state. |
112	| `fmt: compact=false scope=file` | File | Disable compaction throughout the current YAML document or one source-file hashpipe YAML block. |
113	| `fmt: table` | Next | Align the next compatible sequence of flow mappings. |
114	| `fmt: compact table` | Next | Collapse eligible block mapping rows before aligning them. `fmt: table compact` and `fmt: table compact=true` are equivalent. |
115	
116	`fmt: table` accepts only its default next-target scope. Compact directives
117	accept `next`, `from-here`, and `file`.

119	`compact`, `compact=true`, `compact=yes`, `compact=1`, and `compact true`
120	enable compaction. `compact=false`, `compact=no`, `compact=0`, and

123	## Templates and embedded formatters
124	
125	| Directive | Scope | Effect |
126	| --- | --- | --- |
127	| `fmt: template.delimiters "<<" ">>"` | Inferred | Add one non-empty double-quoted delimiter pair using the placement rule below. |
128	| `fmt: template.delimiters "<<" ">>" scope=next` | Next | Add the pair to the next supported target. |
129	| `fmt: template.delimiters "<<" ">>" scope=from-here` | From here | Add the pair to following supported targets. |
130	| `fmt: template.delimiters "<<" ">>" scope=file` | File | Add the pair throughout the current document or nested region. |
131	| `fmt: embedded python` | Next | Format the next supported string or YAML literal scalar with the named formatter. |
132	| `fmt: python` | Next | Shorthand for `fmt: embedded python`. |

134	A bare `fmt: template.delimiters` directive uses the next target when placed
135	directly before one. When blank lines or range boundaries isolate it from
136	content on both sides, it applies from there onward. The directive requires an
137	explicit scope in every other placement.

139	Delimiter arguments must be non-empty double-quoted tokens; single quotes are
140	not accepted. Inside a token, `\"`, `\\`, `\n`, `\r`, and `\t` represent a
141	double quote, backslash, newline, carriage return, and tab.

143	Embedded formatter directives accept only `scope=next`. The name can select a
144	built-in alias or an entry from [`[embedded]`](reference-config.qmd#embedded).

146	YAML can also mark a scalar as Markdown with the `!markdown` or `!md` tag:
147	
148	```yaml

150	```

18	| Markdown fences named `yaml`, `yml`, `markdown`, or `md` | YAML, or recursively formatted Markdown. | Automatic unless the fence is locally skipped. |
19	| Markdown source fences | Python, R, JSON, GraphQL, CSS, HTML, JavaScript, TypeScript, and related aliases. | Delegated when a matching embedded formatter is available. |
