23	
24	Extension matching is ASCII case-insensitive. In path mode, unsupported
25	extensions are counted as skipped and do not make the run fail. An unsupported
26	`--stdin-file-path` is an error because stdin mode requires file-aware behavior.

28	Directory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`,
29	and global Git ignore files. Passing a hidden path explicitly selects it.

31	## JSON-to-YAML projection
32	
33	Formatting preserves the source language and produces output that can replace
34	the input. JSON-to-YAML projection has a different contract: it parses a
35	JSON-family input and emits formatted YAML for inspection or conversion.
36	
37	Use `yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path` to project JSON-family input from stdin
38	to formatted YAML on stdout:
39	
40	```sh
41	yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json < data.json
42	```
43	
44	The command does not read or write the path. It uses the extension to select
45	one exact input grammar:
46	
47	| Extension | Accepted input |
48	| --- | --- |
49	| `.json` | Strict JSON. |
50	| `.jsonc` | JSON with line comments, block comments, and trailing commas. Other JSON5 syntax is rejected. |
51	| `.json5` | JSON5 strings, identifiers, numbers, comments, and trailing commas. |
52	| `.jsonl` and `.ndjson` | One strict JSON value per physical line. Blank records are rejected. |
53	
54	Object member order and duplicate names are preserved. JSON and JSONC keep the
55	source spelling of numbers. JSON5 spellings that YAML would interpret
56	differently are normalized, including `0X` hexadecimal prefixes, leading or
57	trailing decimal points, unary plus, `Infinity`, and `NaN`. Negative
58	hexadecimal integers are emitted in decimal because YAML would otherwise treat
59	them as strings.
60	
61	JSONC and JSON5 comments become YAML comments. JSONL and NDJSON output a YAML
62	document-start marker before every record. A record may be an object, array, or
63	scalar; this does not change how ordinary YAML such as `1\n2` is interpreted by
64	`yamark format`.
65	
66	String escapes are decoded before YAML emission. Lone UTF-16 surrogate escapes
67	are rejected because they do not represent Unicode scalar values. All
68	JSON-family inputs reject nesting deeper than 256 levels. JSON5 also rejects
69	legacy numeric escapes such as `\1`, invalid escaped identifier characters, and
70	U+0085 as whitespace. Characters that YAML cannot carry inside a comment are
71	shown as visible hexadecimal escapes.
72	
73	Projection does not scan JSON strings or comments for embedded Markdown or
74	formatter directives, and it does not dispatch to Prettier or another embedded
75	formatter.
76	
77	`yamark format` continues to skip JSON-family paths and never rewrites them.
78	`Yamark: View JSON as YAML` in VS Code and Positron uses the same JSON-to-YAML
79	projection.

136	### JSON Lines (JSONL) as YAML streams
137	
138	Path-aware formatting recognizes a `.yaml` or `.yml` stream made of two or more
139	unmarked, one-line YAML flow-mapping roots, one per physical line with no
140	separate trivia lines. It inserts the `---` document-start marker before every
141	record, including the first.
142	
143	JSON objects are the common case, but the trigger is based on YAML shape and is
144	not restricted to strict JSON objects.
145	
146	Normal `--line-width` rules still determine whether each record and its nested
147	collections stay in flow style or expand to block style. A single flow-mapping
148	root or a stream containing any non-flow-mapping root follows the normal YAML
149	path instead.
150	
151	See the generated [JSON Lines example](examples.qmd#json-lines-as-a-yaml-stream).

212	## Layout repair
213	
214	Yamark recognizes two narrow layout cues. Only the unmatched opener is a repair
215	for ill-formed input:
216	
217	- An unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping begins as a mapping
218	  value or sequence item asks Yamark to collapse that one collection to flow
219	  style.
220	- A physical newline inside a complete flow collection is valid multiline YAML.
221	  It asks Yamark to expand that collection to block style. Compact mode
222	  suppresses this multiline intent.
223	
224	The opener may be on the value line or on the following line after an empty
225	mapping value header. Adjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not
226	layout hints.
227	
228	When the requested flow form fits the available `--line-width`, Yamark removes
229	the unmatched opener and emits the collection in flow style. Otherwise it
230	preserves the hinted collection as typed. It does not fail solely because the
231	requested flow form is too wide, and surrounding YAML may still be formatted.
232	The [layout examples](examples.qmd#collapse-to-flow-by-typing-a-bracket) show
233	each accepted gesture before and after formatting.
234	
235	## Failure behavior
236	
237	Yamark is a formatter, not a general validator. It formats supported regions
238	and leaves unsupported regions unchanged when they are not explicitly
239	targeted and it has no safe rewrite.
240	
241	Yamark parses YAML before formatting. For Markdown and Markdown-valued YAML
242	scalars, it emits only transformations supported by its parser. An embedded
243	formatter can change only a recognized fence or an explicitly marked source or
244	YAML target.
245	
246	An explicit directive instead requires a supported target. A missing or
247	unsupported target or an unknown formatter name is an error for that file.
248	Formatter execution follows the optional and strict failure rules above.
249	
250	Input-decoding, parsing, formatting, file-read, and external-formatter errors
251	happen before Yamark writes that file, so these errors leave its original
252	content unchanged. A write error is reported, but writes are direct rather than
253	atomic; Yamark does not promise rollback after a write begins.
254	
255	A multi-file write run is not transactional. Other files can be written even
256	when one input fails.

35	### Table widths
36	
37	`fit` sizes supported pipe, simple, grid, and multiline table columns from
38	their contents, with consistent padding. It can shrink excessive widths or
39	expand cramped columns. Both modes preserve column alignment and multiline
40	cell breaks.
41	
42	`preserve` retains the source widths while still formatting cell contents.
43	For Pandoc tables, this keeps the borders and gaps that determine widths. For
44	pipe tables, it keeps separator lengths and row widths, even when the original
45	rows are not aligned with one another.
46	
47	Pandoc can use source widths to determine rendered column proportions and
48	wrapping. Choose `preserve` when those widths are intentional:
49	
50	```markdown
51	<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->
52	+----------+------------------+
53	| Name     | Description      |
54	+==========+==================+
55	| A        | Short text       |
56	+----------+------------------+
57	```
58	
59	Use `scope=file` for a document-wide choice or `scope=from-here` for subsequent
60	tables. A later `table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths.
61	Without an explicit scope, this option follows the usual Markdown directive
62	default of `scope=file`.
63	
64	The setting also works in front matter, `yamark.toml`, and the command line.
65	Explicit renderer settings such as Quarto's `tbl-colwidths` remain unchanged.
66	`fmt: skip` preserves the entire table when exact source layout matters.
67	Unsupported table structures remain unchanged in either mode.

69	### Canonical and footnote values
70	
71	`canonical` accepts `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0` in front matter
72	and directives. A bare `canonical` directive means `canonical=true`. Canonical
73	mode rewrites supported `_emphasis_` and `__strong__` spans as `*emphasis*` and
74	`**strong**`. It preserves protected or unsupported spans, including intraword
75	underscores, code spans, link destinations, raw HTML, and template content.
76	
77	For `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` format footnote
78	definitions. `preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` preserve them.
79	`--preserve-footnotes` preserves Markdown footnote definitions byte-for-byte.

100	| `--diagnostics` | For YAML input, emits trace counters; it also emits notes for skipped or failing optional embedded formatters. |
101	| `--skip-embedded-formatters` | Disables external formatters while keeping Yamark's Markdown, YAML, front matter, and recursive Markdown formatting active. |
102	| `--config <path>` | Uses one explicit `yamark.toml` for all selected files instead of discovering one per file. |

105	
106	| Need | Control |

108	| Select a target | Use a recognized Markdown fence language or a [`fmt: <name>` directive](reference-directives.qmd#templates-and-embedded-formatters). |
109	| Register or replace a formatter | Add an [`[embedded.<name>]` table](reference-config.qmd#embedded) to `yamark.toml`. |
110	| Disable external formatters for one run | Pass `--skip-embedded-formatters`. |
111	| Explain an optional formatter skip | Pass `--diagnostics`. |

116	## Document Markdown options
117	
118	Markdown front matter can set document-local options under
119	`editor_options.markdown`:
120	
121	```markdown
122	---
123	editor_options:
124	  markdown:
125	    wrap: sentence:72
126	    canonical: true
127	    footnotes: preserve
128	    table-widths: preserve
129	---
130	This is __strong__. This is _emphasis_.
131	```
132	
133	| Key | Accepted values |
134	| --- | --- |
135	| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer column. |
136	| `table-widths` | `fit` or `preserve`. |
137	| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |
138	| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |
139	
140	Unknown front-matter keys and unrecognized values are ignored; the
141	corresponding base setting remains active. Invalid `yamark.toml` keys or
142	directive values are errors instead.
143	
144	These options apply after the front matter to the Markdown body, recursive
145	`markdown` or `md` fences, and Markdown-valued YAML scalars in nested YAML
146	regions.
147	
148	Yamark also reads `editor.markdown` for compatibility, but only when
149	`editor_options.markdown` is absent. It does not merge the two tables. Git
150	filter subcommands use their own wrapping options and do not read document
151	options.
152	
153	## Interaction rules
154	
155	Markdown settings are applied in this order:
156	
157	1. Command defaults and config establish the base settings. Explicit `--wrap`
158	   and `--table-widths` values override their corresponding `[format]` config
159	   values.
160	2. Document front matter overrides the corresponding base Markdown settings
161	   for the document body and its nested Markdown regions.
162	3. Directives then override the corresponding settings within their scope.
163	4. `--preserve-footnotes` is the final exception: it preserves footnote
164	   definitions even when front matter or a directive requests formatting.
165	
166	Other interactions:
167	
168	- `--compact` enables compact mode even if `[format].compact` is `false`. A
169	  scoped `fmt: compact=false` directive can disable it for its target, region,
170	  or file.
171	- `editor_options.markdown` takes the place of the compatibility
172	  `editor.markdown` table when both are present; the tables are not merged.
173	- Git filter clean and smudge commands use their own Markdown wrapping options.
174	  They do not read document Markdown options.

15	## YAML and Markdown documents
16	
17	### Markdown with YAML front matter
18	
19	Agent skills and prompt files can put structured metadata above free-form
20	Markdown. Yamark formats both in one pass.
21	
22	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
23	**Before**
24	
25	```markdown
26	---
27	name: review-pr
28	description: Review a pull request and recommend changes inline with the project's style guide, focusing on correctness, readability, and tests.
29	tags: [review,pull-request,code]
30	---

32	#   Review ##
33	
34	Read the diff and flag anything that violates the style guide, has obvious correctness issues, or looks untested. Prefer specific suggestions over vague concerns.
35	```
36	
37	**After**
38	
39	```markdown
40	---
41	name: review-pr
42	description: >-
43	  Review a pull request and recommend changes inline with the project's
44	  style guide, focusing on correctness, readability, and tests.
45	tags: [review, pull-request, code]
46	---
47	
48	# Review
49	
50	Read the diff and flag anything that violates the style guide, has
51	obvious correctness issues, or looks untested. Prefer specific
52	suggestions over vague concerns.
53	```
54	::::
55	
56	### Markdown in YAML {#markdown-valued-yaml-scalars}
57	
58	Yamark can format Markdown stored in YAML in three ways: tag the value with
59	`!markdown`, use `!md` as a shorter alias, or put `# fmt: markdown` on the line
60	before the value. The example below shows the full tag and comment forms.
61	
62	A `prompts.yaml` or `agents.yaml` file can use any of these forms. Yamark wraps
63	the selected value as Markdown, choosing folded or literal block style from the
64	content.
65	
66	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
67	**Before**
68	
69	```yaml
70	agents:
71	  reviewer:
72	    instructions: !markdown "Focus on correctness and tests. Flag any change that lacks a regression test. Prefer concrete suggestions: name the function, name the case."
73	  summarizer:
74	    # fmt: markdown
75	    instructions: |
76	      You write release notes.
77	
78	      - One bullet per user-visible change.
79	      - No internal refactors.
80	```
81	
82	**After**
83	
84	```yaml
85	agents:
86	  reviewer:
87	    instructions: !markdown |
88	      Focus on correctness and tests. Flag any change that lacks a regression
89	      test. Prefer concrete suggestions: name the function, name the case.
90	  summarizer:
91	    # fmt: markdown
92	    instructions: |
93	      You write release notes.
94	
95	      - One bullet per user-visible change.
96	      - No internal refactors.
97	```
98	::::
99	
100	The tagged value contains only prose, so Yamark rewraps it as a folded block.
101	The comment-marked value contains a list, so Yamark keeps literal block style
102	(`|`) because folding would destroy the line breaks Markdown depends on.
103	
104	### Source code in YAML
105	
106	YAML values can also contain source code. Use `# fmt: python`, `# fmt: r`, or
107	the name of another configured formatter before a literal block. When the
108	formatter is available, Yamark formats the block and restores its indentation
109	in the YAML file.
110	
111	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
112	**Before**
113	
114	```yaml
115	# fmt: python
116	preflight: |
117	  def check(items):return all(x>0 for x in items)
118	```
119	
120	**After**
121	
122	```yaml
123	# fmt: python
124	preflight: |
125	  def check(items):
126	    return all(x > 0 for x in items)
127	```
128	::::
129	
130	### YAML scalar presentation
131	
132	Yamark changes scalar spelling only when the parsed YAML value and tag
133	stay equivalent. It can simplify safe quoted strings, keep strings that
134	would be misread as booleans, convert hard newlines to literal blocks,
135	and fold long prose strings.
136	
137	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
138	**Before**
139	
140	```yaml
141	title: "hello"
142	boolish: "true"
143	body: "alpha\nbeta\n"
144	summary: "This package formats YAML front matter and configuration files while preserving semantics, comments, and repository-friendly diffs."
145	```
146	
147	**After**
148	
149	```yaml
150	title: hello
151	boolish: "true"
152	body: |
153	  alpha
154	  beta
155	summary: >-
156	  This package formats YAML front matter and configuration files while
157	  preserving semantics, comments, and repository-friendly diffs.
158	```
159	::::

162

164	definitions wrap under the marker unless the document or CLI asks to

194	always use compact pipe-table output.

216	## Markdown in source files
217	
218	### Hashpipe YAML in source files
219	
220	Consecutive own-line `#|` comments in Python and R are a YAML block. Yamark
221	formats the comment body as YAML, restores the hashpipe prefix, and leaves the
222	surrounding source code unchanged. This recognition is automatic; it does not
223	need a `fmt:` directive.
224	
225	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
226	**Before**
227	
228	```r
229	#| name: demo
230	#| launcher:
231	#|  vanilla: true
232	#|  default-packages: [base,utils]
233	
234	main <- function() NULL
235	```
236	
237	**After**
238	
239	```r
240	#| name: demo
241	#| launcher:
242	#|   vanilla: true
243	#|   default-packages: [base, utils]
244	
245	main <- function() NULL
246	```
247	::::
248	
249	### Embedded Markdown in Python
250	
251	When a prompt lives next to the code that uses it, Yamark can format the prose
252	without changing the surrounding Python. Add `# fmt: markdown` before the
253	string:
254	
255	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
256	**Before**
257	
258	```python
259	# fmt: markdown
260	REVIEW_PROMPT = """
261	# Review
262	
263	Read the diff and flag anything that violates the style guide, has obvious correctness issues, or looks untested.
264	
265	-   Prefer specific suggestions over vague concerns.
266	-   Name the function and the case.
267	"""
268	```
269	
270	**After**
271	
272	```python
273	# fmt: markdown
274	REVIEW_PROMPT = """
275	# Review
276	
277	Read the diff and flag anything that violates the style guide, has
278	obvious correctness issues, or looks untested.
279	
280	- Prefer specific suggestions over vague concerns.
281	- Name the function and the case.
282	"""
283	```
284	::::
285	
286	Python source outside the marked string is left untouched. Run `ruff format` for
287	that.
288	
289	### Embedded Markdown in source comments
290	
291	The same directive can target a contiguous source comment block. This is useful
292	for generated help text or documentation snippets where a string literal is not
293	the right host.
294	
295	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
296	**Before**
297	
298	```python
299	# fmt: markdown
300	# #   Filters
301	#
302	# Apply one or more filters. Put the most specific filter first.
303	#
304	# -   Each filter is a single expression.
305	```
306	
307	**After**
308	
309	```python
310	# fmt: markdown
311	# # Filters
312	#
313	# Apply one or more filters. Put the most specific filter first.
314	#
315	# - Each filter is a single expression.
316	```
317	::::
318	
319	### Embedded Markdown in R
320	
321	The same pattern works for R raw strings. It can format package vignettes,
322	documentation fragments, and Shiny help text kept next to the code that renders
323	it.
324	
325	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
326	**Before**
327	
328	```r
329	# fmt: markdown
330	help_text <- r"(
331	# Filters
332	
333	Apply one or more filters. Filters are evaluated top-to-bottom; the first match wins, so put the most specific filter first.
334	
335	-   Each filter is a single expression.
336	-   Multiple filters combine with AND.
337	)"
338	```
339	
340	**After**
341	
342	```r
343	# fmt: markdown
344	help_text <- r"(
345	# Filters
346	
347	Apply one or more filters. Filters are evaluated top-to-bottom; the
348	first match wins, so put the most specific filter first.
349	
350	- Each filter is a single expression.
351	- Multiple filters combine with AND.
352	)"
353	```
354	::::
355	
356	## YAML layout
357	
358	### JSON Lines as a YAML stream
359	
360	Give a JSON Lines file containing two or more object records a `.yaml` or
361	`.yml` extension, with one record per line, then format it normally. Yamark
362	inserts a leading `---` document-start marker before every record, including
363	the first, producing a valid YAML multi-document stream. The example below uses
364	records from agent runs.
365	
366	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
367	**Before**
368	
369	```yaml
370	{"id":1,"profile":{"name":"planner","active":true}}
371	{"id":2,"profile":{"name":"researcher","active":true},"usage":{"input_tokens":640,"output_tokens":128}}
372	{"id":3,"profile":{"name":"reviewer","active":true,"model":"gpt-5","region":"us","tools":["search","python"]},"events":[{"type":"tool_call","tools":["search","open","python","write"]},{"type":"usage","tokens":{"input":900,"output":240}},{"type":"completion","status":"ok"}]}
373	```
374	
375	**After**
376	
377	```yaml
378	---
379	{id: 1, profile: {name: planner, active: true}}
380	---
381	id: 2
382	profile: {name: researcher, active: true}
383	usage: {input_tokens: 640, output_tokens: 128}
384	---
385	id: 3
386	profile:
387	  name: reviewer
388	  active: true
389	  model: gpt-5
390	  region: us
391	  tools: [search, python]
392	events:
393	  - {type: tool_call, tools: [search, open, python, write]}
394	  - {type: usage, tokens: {input: 900, output: 240}}
395	  - {type: completion, status: ok}
396	```
397	::::
398	
399	Yamark keeps each document as compact as the width allows. The first record
400	stays in flow style; the second expands only its root mapping; the third also
401	expands `profile` and `events`. Smaller mappings and sequences remain in flow
402	style whenever they still fit within `--line-width`. This conversion is for
403	object records, not arbitrary JSON values.
404	
405	### Aligned flow-mapping tables
406	
407	A sequence of similar flow mappings can be easier to scan as a table. Mark it
408	with `# fmt: table` and Yamark aligns columns by key:
409	
410	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
411	**Before**
412	
413	```yaml
414	# fmt: table
415	- {name: alpha,type: string,default: [one,two],description: "Short"}
416	- {name: beta,type: int,default: 0,description: "Number"}
417	```
418	
419	**After**
420	
421	```yaml
422	# fmt: table
423	- {name: alpha, type: string, default: [one, two], description: Short}
424	- {name: beta,  type: int,    default: 0,          description: Number}
425	```
426	::::
427	
428	### Compact collections
429	
430	Short, simple block collections can read better as a single flow line.
431	Enable `compact = true` in `yamark.toml` (or pass `--compact`) and
432	Yamark collapses eligible block mappings and sequences that fit the
433	structural width:
434	
435	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
436	**Before**
437	
438	```yaml
439	tags:
440	  - yaml
441	  - markdown
442	  - docs
443	package:
444	  name: yamark
445	  language: rust
446	```
447	
448	**After**
449	
450	```yaml
451	tags: [yaml, markdown, docs]
452	package: {name: yamark, language: rust}
453	```
454	::::
455	
456	Collections with comments, aliases, tags, anchors, multiline scalars, or
457	block scalars stay in block style.
458	
459	### Collapse to flow by typing a bracket
460	
461	Drop an unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping value starts and
462	Yamark reads it as a layout hint: collapse this collection onto one line. The
463	file doesn't parse as you typed it, but the intent is obvious - Yamark removes
464	the opener and emits flow style.
465	
466	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
467	**Before**
468	
469	```yaml
470	tags: [
471	  - yaml
472	  - markdown
473	  - docs
474	```
475	
476	**After**
477	
478	```yaml
479	tags: [yaml, markdown, docs]
480	```
481	::::
482	
483	The opener may also be detached onto the next line after an empty mapping value
484	header:
485	
486	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
487	**Before**
488	
489	```yaml
490	tags:
491	[
492	  - yaml
493	  - markdown
494	  - docs
495	```
496	
497	**After**
498	
499	```yaml
500	tags: [yaml, markdown, docs]
501	```
502	::::
503	
504	Adjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not repaired as layout hints.
505	
506	A newline inside an existing flow collection requests the reverse change: expand
507	the collection to block style.
508	
509	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
510	**Before**
511	
512	```yaml
513	- {a: b,
514	   c: d}
515	```
516	
517	**After**
518	
519	```yaml
520	- a: b
521	  c: d
522	```
523	::::
524	
525	See [Supported files and syntax -> Layout repair](reference-files.qmd#layout-repair)
526	for the acceptance rules.
527	
528	## Fenced and nested content
529	
530	### Recursive Markdown code fences
531	
532	YAML fences are formatted as YAML. Markdown fences are formatted
533	recursively, so nested YAML inside nested Markdown is formatted too.
534	
535	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
536	**Before**
537	
538	`````markdown
539	```yaml
540	# fmt: table
541	- {name: a,type: int,default: 0}
542	- {name: long_name,type: string,default: ""}
543	```
544	
545	````markdown
546	#   Inner
547	
548	```yaml
549	items: [a,b]
550	```
551	````
552	`````
553	
554	**After**
555	
556	`````markdown
557	```yaml
558	# fmt: table
559	- {name: a,         type: int,    default: 0}
560	- {name: long_name, type: string, default: ""}
561	```
562	
563	````markdown
564	# Inner
565	
566	```yaml
567	items: [a, b]
568	```
569	````
570	`````
571	::::
572	
573	### Prettier-backed web and data fences
574	
575	When `prettier` is on `PATH`, JSON, JSONC, JSON5, GraphQL, CSS, SCSS, Less,
576	PostCSS, HTML, JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, and TSX fenced blocks are handed to
577	it. Python and R fences go to Ruff and Air the same way:
578	
579	:::: {.showcase-before-after}
580	**Before**
581	
582	````markdown
583	```json
584	{"name":"yamark","tags":["yaml","markdown","formatter"],"engines":{"node":">=18"}}
585	```
586	
587	```ts
588	function format(input:string):string{return input.trim()}
589	```
590	````
591	
592	**After**
593	
594	````markdown
595	```json
596	{
597	  "name": "yamark",
598	  "tags": ["yaml", "markdown", "formatter"],
599	  "engines": { "node": ">=18" }
600	}
601	```
602	
603	```ts
604	function format(input: string): string {
605	  return input.trim();
606	}
607	```
608	````
609	::::
610	
611	A missing `prettier` leaves the fence unchanged. Override or disable a
612	language with `[embedded.<language>]` in `yamark.toml`, or skip them all with
613	`--skip-embedded-formatters`.
614

# CI for the Riverton Open Data Portal
#
#  * validates every dataset descriptor under datasets/
#  * runs the harvester test-suite on several Python versions and OSes
#  * builds the static "explore" site and, on tags, publishes it to Pages

name: "CI"

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    paths-ignore: ['docs/**', '**/*.md', 'explore/static/**', '.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**', 'LICENSE', 'CITATION.cff']
  pull_request:
    branches:
    - main
  schedule:
      # Every Monday 04:30 UTC: re-validate the upstream department feeds
      - cron: '30 4 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dataset:
        description: Validate only this dataset slug (leave it empty to validate the whole catalogue, which takes about twenty minutes)
        required: false
        default: ""
      publish:
        description: "Publish the site after a successful build?"
        type: boolean
        default: False

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  PORTAL_ENV: ci
  CKAN_API_URL: https://data.riverton.gov/api/3/action
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
  UV_VERSION: "0.4.30"
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"
  TZ: America/Chicago

jobs:

  validate-datasets:
    name: Validate dataset descriptors
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - &checkout
        name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Install validator
        run: pipx install "frictionless==5.18.0"

      - name: Validate
        # the dataset input is only set for manual runs
        run: |
          if [ -n "${{ github.event.inputs.dataset }}" ]; then
            frictionless validate "datasets/${{ github.event.inputs.dataset }}/datapackage.json"
          else
            for pkg in datasets/*/datapackage.json; do
              frictionless validate "$pkg" || exit 1
            done
          fi

    needs: validate-datasets
    name: Tests (${{ matrix.os }}, py${{ matrix.python-version }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}
    strategy:
       fail-fast: False
       max-parallel: 4

         os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-14]
         python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
         experimental: [false]
         include:
           - { os: ubuntu-latest, python-version: "3.14-dev", experimental: true }
           - {os: ubuntu-24.04-arm,python-version: "3.12",experimental: true}

           # the 3.10 macOS runners keep timing out on the GDAL wheel
           - os: macos-14
             python-version: "3.10"

# ShiftShare -- volunteer scheduling for the Riverton Community Food Bank and partners
# Written by hand (no Helm chart yet). Apply with:
#   kubectl apply -f deploy/shiftshare.yaml
---
# Namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: shiftshare
  labels:
    team: "volunteer-services"
    cost-centre: '4410'
---

# Non-secret configuration. Values must be strings, hence all the quotes.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
    name: shiftshare-config
    namespace: shiftshare
    annotations:
        shiftshare.riverton.org/last-reviewed: "2026-08-12"
        shiftshare.riverton.org/owner: Volunteer Services (Mon-Fri, 9-5)
data:
    APP_ENV: production
    APP_URL: https://volunteer.riverton.org
    DEFAULT_TIMEZONE: "America/Chicago"
    REMINDER_HOURS_BEFORE: "24"
    MAX_SHIFTS_PER_WEEK: "6"
    FEATURE_SMS_REMINDERS: "true"
    FEATURE_WAITLIST: 'false'
    welcome-email.txt: |
        Hi {{ volunteer.first_name }},

        Thanks for signing up to volunteer with {{ org.name }}! Your first shift is on
        {{ shift.starts_at | date("l j F") }} at {{ site.name }}.

        If you can't make it, please cancel at least 24 hours ahead so someone on the waitlist can take your place.
    motd.txt: |+
        Scheduled maintenance: Sundays 02:00-03:00 (America/Chicago).

    policy-summary.md: >
        Volunteers under 16 must be accompanied by a registered adult.
        Shifts at the warehouse require closed-toe shoes.

        Background checks are required only for roles that involve
        working with children or vulnerable adults; see the Safeguarding policy for the full list of roles affected by this requirement.
---
# Placeholders only! The real values live in the sealed-secrets repo.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata: {name: shiftshare-secrets, namespace: shiftshare}
type: Opaque
stringData:
  DATABASE_URL: postgres://shiftshare:CHANGEME@shiftshare-db.shiftshare.svc:5432/shiftshare
  TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN: !!str 0123456789
  SESSION_SECRET: "replace-me"
  SMTP_PASSWORD: ""

---
# Web application (Laravel). Two replicas is plenty outside of
# the November/December holiday drive.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shiftshare-web
  namespace: shiftshare
  labels: &web-labels
    app.kubernetes.io/name: shiftshare
    app.kubernetes.io/component: web
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: "shiftshare"
spec:
  replicas: !!int "2"
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels: *web-labels
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate: { maxSurge: 1 ,maxUnavailable: 0 }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        <<: *web-labels
        tier: frontend
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "9253"
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: no
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 1000, fsGroup: 1000}
      nodeSelector: ~
      affinity:
      containers:
      -   name: web
          image: ghcr.io/riverton-food-bank/shiftshare:3.2.0
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          args: ["php-fpm", "--nodaemonize", "--fpm-config", "/usr/local/etc/php-fpm.d/www.conf", "--force-stderr"]
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
              protocol: TCP
            - {name: metrics, containerPort: 9253}
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef: { name: shiftshare-config }
            - secretRef:
                name: shiftshare-secrets
          env:
            - name: POD_IP
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef: {fieldPath: status.podIP}
            # queue name must match the CronJob further down
            - name: QUEUE_NAME
              value: "reminders"
            - name: LOG_CHANNEL
              value: stderr
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 250m ,memory: 256Mi }
            limits:   {cpu: "1", memory: 512Mi}
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: http}
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            failureThreshold: 3
          securityContext:
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: True
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
# Cluster-internal service for the web pods
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: shiftshare-web
  namespace: shiftshare
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: shiftshare
    app.kubernetes.io/component: web
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: http
---
# Public entry point. TLS via cert-manager; the old hostname keeps working until 2027.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: shiftshare
  namespace: shiftshare
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: "letsencrypt-prod"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size: 10m
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet: |
      more_set_headers "X-Robots-Tag: noindex";
      more_set_headers "Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=()";
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/server-alias: "volunteers.riverton.org, www.volunteer.riverton.org"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts: [ volunteer.riverton.org, volunteers.riverton.org ]
      secretName: shiftshare-tls
  rules:
    - host: volunteer.riverton.org
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: shiftshare-web
                port: {name: http}
---
# Sends the "your shift is tomorrow" reminders. Runs hourly; the app decides who
# is due a reminder, so an overlapping run is harmless (but wasteful).
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: shiftshare-reminders
  namespace: shiftshare
spec:
  schedule: "5 * * * *"
  timeZone: America/Chicago
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 5
  suspend: false
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 2
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
            - name: reminders
              image: ghcr.io/riverton-food-bank/shiftshare:3.2.0
              command: ["php", "artisan", "shifts:send-reminders", "--hours=24", "--channel=sms,email", "--quiet"]
              envFrom:
                - configMapRef: {name: shiftshare-config}
                - secretRef: {name: shiftshare-secrets}
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: shiftshare-web
  namespace: shiftshare
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: shiftshare, app.kubernetes.io/component: web}

# ShiftShare public API
# Source of truth for the volunteer portal, the kiosk app and partner integrations.
# Lint with:  npx @redocly/cli lint openapi.yaml
openapi: "3.1.0"
info:
  title: ShiftShare Volunteer Scheduling API
  version: "3.2"
  summary: 'Book, swap and cancel volunteer shifts at Riverton''s community organisations.'
  description: |
    The ShiftShare API lets partner organisations (food banks, libraries, shelters, the parks department) publish volunteer shifts and lets volunteers book them.

    ## Authentication
    All write operations need a bearer token issued by the partner admin console.  Read-only endpoints for **published** shifts are public, but are rate limited to 60 requests per minute per IP address.

    ## Conventions
    * Times are ISO 8601 with an offset, e.g. `2026-03-14T09:00:00-05:00`.
    * Lists are paginated with `cursor` / `limit`.
    * Personal data (phone numbers, dates of birth) is never returned to other volunteers.
  contact:
    name: Volunteer Services digital team
    email: shiftshare@riverton.org
    url: https://volunteer.riverton.org/developers
  license: { name: AGPL-3.0-or-later, url: "https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.html" }
  x-last-reviewed: 2026-10-28

servers:
- url: https://api.volunteer.riverton.org/v3
  description: Production
- url: "https://staging-api.volunteer.riverton.org/v3"
  description: Staging (data is reset every night at 02:00)
- url: http://localhost:{port}/v3
  description: Local development
  variables:
    port:
      default: "8080"
      enum: ["8080", "8000", "3000"]

tags:
  - name: shifts
    description: Volunteer shifts offered by partner organisations.
  - name: bookings
    description: 'A volunteer''s booking of a shift, including waitlist entries.'
  - name: organisations
    x-displayName: Partner organisations

security:
  - bearerAuth: []

paths:
  /shifts:
    get:
      tags: [shifts]
      summary: List published shifts
      operationId: listShifts
      security: []        # public endpoint
      parameters:
        - name: from
          in: query
          description: Only return shifts starting on or after this date.
          schema: { type: string, format: date }
          example: 2026-03-14
        - name: organisation
          in: query
          schema: {type: string}

        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Cursor'
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A page of shifts.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ShiftPage'
        "429": &rateLimited
          description: Too many requests. Slow down and retry after the number of seconds given in the Retry-After response header.
          headers:
            Retry-After: {schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1}}
      x-amazon-apigateway-integration:
        type: aws_proxy
        httpMethod: POST
        uri: !Sub "arn:aws:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/${ShiftsFunction.Arn}/invocations"
        credentials: !Ref ApiGatewayInvokeRole
    post:
      tags: [ shifts ]
      summary: Publish a new shift
      operationId: createShift
      requestBody:
        required: True
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/ShiftInput' }
            examples:
              pantry:
                summary: Saturday pantry shift
                value: {organisation_id: 12, title: "Pantry sorting", starts_at: "2026-03-14T09:00:00-05:00", ends_at: "2026-03-14T12:00:00-05:00", capacity: 8}
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'
        "429": *rateLimited

  /shifts/{shiftId}/bookings:
    parameters:
      - name: shiftId
        in: path
        required: yes
        schema:
          type: integer
          format: int64
    post:
      tags:
      - bookings
      summary: Book a shift (or join its waitlist)
      description: >-
        Creates a booking for the authenticated volunteer.
        If the shift is full and has a waitlist, the volunteer is added to the
        waitlist instead and the response status is `202`.


        Volunteers can hold at most six upcoming bookings; the seventh attempt returns `409 Conflict`.
      operationId: bookShift
      responses:
        "201": {description: Booked}
        "202": {description: Added to the waitlist}
        "409": { description: "Booking limit reached, or already booked" }
      deprecated: false

components:
  parameters:
    Cursor:
      name: cursor
      in: query
      required: false
      schema: {type: string}
    Limit:
      name: limit
      in: query
      schema: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 25 }
  responses:
    ValidationError:
      description: The request body failed validation.
  schemas:
    ShiftInput:
      type: object
      required: [organisation_id, title, starts_at, ends_at]
      properties:
        organisation_id: {type: integer}
        title:
          type: string
          maxLength: 120
          example: "Pantry sorting"
        starts_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        ends_at:   { type: string, format: date-time }
        capacity: {type: integer, minimum: 1, default: 1}
        days: {type: array, items: {type: string, enum: [monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday, sunday, public-holiday]}}
        min_age:
          type: [integer, "null"]
          default: ~
          description: Minimum volunteer age for this shift, or null when there is no restriction beyond the organisation's own policy.
        contact_phone:
          type: string
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()-]{7,20}$'
        check_in_time: {type: string, example: "08:30"}
        notes:
    Shift:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/ShiftInput'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id: {type: integer, format: int64, readOnly: true}
            status: { type: string, enum: [draft, published, full, cancelled] }
            spots_left: {type: integer}
    ShiftPage:
      type: object
      properties:
        data: {type: array, items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Shift'}}
        next_cursor: {type: ["string", "null"]}
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: JWT

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check how stale the datasets on the Riverton Open Data Portal are.

The portal (CKAN) lists roughly 600 datasets published by 23 city departments.
Each dataset declares an expected update frequency in its metadata; this script
compares that with the last time one of its resources actually changed, and
produces

* a CSV report for the open-data coordinator, and
* a short Markdown summary that is posted to Slack every Monday.

Run ``python freshness.py --help`` for the options. The file also uses the
"percent" cell format so analysts can step through it in VS Code or Jupyter.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import logging
import os
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Iterator

import requests

log = logging.getLogger("freshness")
INTERACTIVE = "ipykernel" in sys.modules

# fmt: markdown
# #   How "stale" is decided
#
# A dataset is **stale** when its newest resource is older than the declared update frequency plus a grace period. The grace period exists because several departments still publish by hand on the first working day of the month, and public holidays push that back.
#
# * `daily` - 2 days of grace
# * `weekly` - 3 days
# *   `monthly` - 10 days
#     * departments on the paper-based process get 5 extra days (see `MANUAL_PUBLISHERS`)
# * anything else (`irregular`, `as needed`, blank) is never flagged
#
# Questions about these numbers go to the open-data coordinator, __not__ to the developers.
GRACE_DAYS = {"daily": 2, "weekly": 3, "monthly": 10, "quarterly": 20, "annually": 45}
PERIOD_DAYS = {"daily": 1, "weekly": 7, "monthly": 31, "quarterly": 92, "annually": 366}
MANUAL_PUBLISHERS = {"parks-and-recreation", "city-clerk", "animal-services"}

CKAN_URL = os.environ.get("CKAN_URL", "https://data.riverton.gov")
REPORT_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("REPORT_DIR", "reports"))


@dataclass
class DatasetStatus:
    name: str
    title: str
    organization: str
    frequency: str
    last_modified: dt.datetime | None
    resources: int = 0
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def age_days(self) -> int | None:
        if self.last_modified is None:
            return None
        return (dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc) - self.last_modified).days

    def is_stale(self) -> bool:
        grace = GRACE_DAYS.get(self.frequency)
        if grace is None or self.age_days is None:
            return False
        if self.organization in MANUAL_PUBLISHERS:
            grace += 5
        return self.age_days > PERIOD_DAYS[self.frequency] + grace


def parse_ckan_time(value: str | None) -> dt.datetime | None:
    """CKAN returns naive ISO timestamps in UTC; make them timezone-aware."""
    if not value:
        return None
    return dt.datetime.fromisoformat(value).replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)


def iter_packages(session: requests.Session, rows: int = 100) -> Iterator[dict]:
    """Yield every public package from CKAN's package_search, page by page."""
    start = 0
    while True:
        resp = session.get(f"{CKAN_URL}/api/3/action/package_search", params={"rows": rows, "start": start}, timeout=30)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        result = resp.json()["result"]
        yield from result["results"]
        start += rows
        if start >= result["count"]:
            break


def to_status(pkg: dict) -> DatasetStatus:
    stamps = [parse_ckan_time(r.get("last_modified") or r.get("created")) for r in pkg.get("resources", [])]
    stamps = [s for s in stamps if s is not None]
    return DatasetStatus(
        name=pkg["name"],
        title=pkg.get("title") or pkg["name"],
        organization=(pkg.get("organization") or {}).get("name", "unknown"),
        frequency=(pkg.get("frequency") or "").strip().lower(),
        last_modified=max(stamps) if stamps else None,
        resources=len(pkg.get("resources", [])),
    )


# fmt: markdown
REPORT_README = r"""
Freshness reports
=================

This folder is written by `freshness.py` every Monday at 06:00.  Each run adds one CSV named `freshness-YYYY-MM-DD.csv`; nothing is deleted automatically, so ask Records Management before you clear it out.

Columns
-------

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | CKAN dataset slug|
| `status` | one of `ok\|stale\|unknown` |
|`age_days`| days since the newest resource changed |

On Windows the share is mapped as `\\cityhall-fs02\OpenData\reports`; on the Linux report server it is mounted at `/mnt/opendata/reports`.

* Do **not** edit the CSVs by hand -- the dashboard reads them.
*  Datasets marked with \* are published manually, so expect them to be late around holidays.
"""

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
SLACK_SUMMARY = """
*Open data freshness report* for the week of {week}. {stale} of {total} datasets are overdue, up from {stale_last_week} last week. The full CSV is on the shared drive; see the README in that folder for what each column means. If a dataset was retired on purpose (e.g. after a department merger), reply in the thread so we can archive it instead of chasing the publisher.
"""


def write_csv(statuses: Iterable[DatasetStatus], path: Path) -> int:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    n = 0
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        writer = csv.writer(fh)
        writer.writerow(["name", "organization", "frequency", "status", "age_days", "resources"])
        for s in statuses:
            status = "unknown" if s.age_days is None else ("stale" if s.is_stale() else "ok")
            writer.writerow([s.name, s.organization, s.frequency or "-", status, s.age_days, s.resources])
            n += 1
    (path.parent / "README.md").write_text(REPORT_README.lstrip(), encoding="utf-8")
    return n


# %% [markdown]
# ## Interactive exploration
# Run the cells below in VS Code or Jupyter to look at a single department.
# Nothing in these cells runs during the Monday job.

# %%
#| label: load-config
#| tags: [ setup,  network ]
#| params:
#|    department:   "public-works"
#|    include_private: no
#|    thresholds: {stale: 1.0, warn: 0.75 }
#| notes: >
#|   Uses the read-only API key; never paste
#|   the admin key into a notebook.
if INTERACTIVE:
    session = requests.Session()
    session.headers["Authorization"] = os.environ.get("CKAN_READONLY_KEY", "")
    department = "public-works"

# %%
#| label: fetch-department
#| echo:   false
#| depends-on:
#|   - load-config
#| output:
#|     format: table
#|     columns: [name,frequency, age_days,  stale]
#|     max-rows: 50
#| caption: "Datasets published by the selected department, sorted by how overdue they are; rows marked ** are stale"
if INTERACTIVE:
    statuses = [to_status(p) for p in iter_packages(session) if (p.get("organization") or {}).get("name") == department]
    statuses.sort(key=lambda s: (not s.is_stale(), -(s.age_days or 0)))
    for s in statuses[:50]:
        print(f"{'**' if s.is_stale() else '  '} {s.name:<45} {s.frequency:<10} {s.age_days}")

# %%
#| label: cli
#| eval: False
#| owner: { team: "Digital Services", contact: opendata@riverton.gov }
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Report stale datasets on the open data portal.")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=REPORT_DIR / f"freshness-{dt.date.today():%Y-%m-%d}.csv")
    parser.add_argument("--fail-on-stale", action="store_true", help="exit with status 1 if anything is stale")
    parser.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG if args.verbose else logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

    with requests.Session() as session:
        statuses = [to_status(p) for p in iter_packages(session)]
    stale = [s for s in statuses if s.is_stale()]
    n = write_csv(statuses, args.out)
    log.info("wrote %d rows to %s (%d stale)", n, args.out, len(stale))
    return 1 if (stale and args.fail_on_stale) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# weekly_respiratory.R
# Riverton County Public Health -- weekly respiratory illness surveillance
#
# Reads the syndromic surveillance extract (ED visits) and the population
# estimates, applies small-cell suppression, and writes the tables behind the
# public dashboard. Run every Monday after the state feed lands (~05:30).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(lubridate)
  library(stringr)
  library(ggplot2)
})

# fmt: markdown
# #  Suppression rules (read before changing anything!)
#
# Counts between 1 and 10 are suppressed in *every* public output, as required by the county's data release policy. Zero is **not** suppressed, because a true zero cannot identify anyone.
#
# 1. Suppress cells with 1-10 events.
# 1. Apply complementary suppression so a hidden value can't be recovered from the row or column totals.
# 1. Rates based on fewer than 20 events are flagged as _unstable_ and drawn in grey.
#
# Ask Dr. Okafor before you change `SUPPRESS_MIN` or `SUPPRESS_MAX`.
SUPPRESS_MIN <- 1L
SUPPRESS_MAX <- 10L
UNSTABLE_BELOW <- 20L

data_dir <- Sys.getenv("SURV_DATA_DIR", "data/raw")
out_dir <- Sys.getenv("SURV_OUT_DIR", "data/public")

#' Suppress small counts in a tidy table
#'
#' Replaces counts between `lo` and `hi` (inclusive) with `NA` and adds a
#' logical `suppressed` column.   Zeros are left alone on purpose.
#'
#' @param df A data frame with an integer `count` column.
#' @param lo,hi Bounds of the suppression window.
#' @return `df` with `count` possibly set to `NA`, plus `suppressed`.
#' @examples
#' suppress_small(tibble::tibble(count = c(0L, 4L, 25L)))
#' @export
suppress_small <- function(df, lo = SUPPRESS_MIN, hi = SUPPRESS_MAX) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      suppressed = !is.na(count) & count >= lo & count <= hi,
      count = if_else(suppressed, NA_integer_, as.integer(count))
    )
}

#' Weekly rate per 100,000 residents
#'
#' @param events Number of events.
#' @param population Mid-year population estimate.
#' @noRd
rate_per_100k <- function(events, population) {
  round(events / population * 1e5, 1)
}

#+ load-data
#| label: load-data
#| message: false
#| cache:   true
#| file-paths:
#|   - "data/raw/ed_visits.csv"
#|   - data/raw/population_estimates_2025.csv
#|   - data/raw/zip_groups.csv
#| col-types: { visit_date: date, zip: character ,count: integer }
#| notes: Population denominators are the state demographer's 2025 vintage; switch to the 2026 vintage once it is published (usually in late spring).
ed_visits <- read_csv(
  file.path(data_dir, "ed_visits.csv"),
  col_types = cols(visit_date = col_date(), zip = col_character(), syndrome = col_character(), count = col_integer())
)
population <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "population_estimates_2025.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
zip_groups <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "zip_groups.csv"), col_types = "cc")

#+ weekly-summary, fig.width = 8
#| label: weekly-summary
#| fig-cap: 'Weekly ED visits for influenza-like illness, by ZIP code group'
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height:   4.5
#| fig-alt: >-
#|     Line chart of weekly emergency department visits for influenza-like illness
#|     in four ZIP code groups since September 2025.
#| syndromes: [ILI,"COVID-like",  RSV-like]
weekly <- ed_visits |>
  filter(syndrome %in% c("ILI", "COVID-like", "RSV-like")) |>
  mutate(week = floor_date(visit_date, unit = "week", week_start = 1)) |>
  left_join(zip_groups, by = "zip") |>
  group_by(week, zip_group, syndrome) |>
  summarise(count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(population, by = "zip_group") |>
  mutate(rate = rate_per_100k(count, population), unstable = count < UNSTABLE_BELOW) |>
  suppress_small()

ggplot(filter(weekly, syndrome == "ILI"), aes(week, rate, colour = zip_group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, unstable), colour = "grey60") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Visits per 100,000", colour = "ZIP group") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# fmt: markdown
dashboard_note <- r"(
## About these numbers

Counts come from emergency department visits where the chief complaint or the discharge diagnosis matches the syndrome definition; they are *not* lab-confirmed cases.  Numbers for the most recent week are **provisional** and usually rise by 5-15% as late records arrive.

-   Cells with 1-10 visits are hidden to protect privacy.
-   Rates are per 100,000 residents.
    Rates based on fewer than 20 visits are shown in grey.
-   ZIP codes are grouped into four areas, see the methods page.

Data source: Riverton County syndromic surveillance system (ESSENCE), updated weekly.
)"

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
email_body <- "
Hello all,

This week's respiratory update is attached. ED visits for influenza-like illness rose for the third week in a row, mostly in the North and Riverside ZIP groups. RSV-like visits are flat. Please check the suppressed cells before you forward anything outside the department.

Thanks, the surveillance team
"

#+ write-outputs
#| label: write-outputs
#| eval: !expr Sys.getenv("SURV_WRITE", "true") == "true"
#| outputs:
#|     csv: data/public/weekly_respiratory.csv
#|     note:  "data/public/about.md"
#| last-reviewed: 2026-09-22
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
weekly |>
  select(week, zip_group, syndrome, count, rate, suppressed, unstable) |>
  arrange(desc(week), zip_group, syndrome) |>
  write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "weekly_respiratory.csv"), na = "")
writeLines(dashboard_note, file.path(out_dir, "about.md"))
message("Wrote ", nrow(weekly), " rows to ", out_dir)

# Changelog
All notable changes to **ShiftShare** are documented in this file.
The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) -- mostly. Volunteer-facing changes are also summarised in plain language in the monthly partner newsletter, which is the place to look if you are a coordinator rather than a developer.

<!-- Add new entries under "Unreleased". Categories: Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed / Security. -->

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- Waitlist position is now shown on the booking page ("You are 3rd on the waitlist").
- Partner admins can export a shift's sign-in sheet as PDF *or* CSV.
* SMS reminders in Spanish and Vietnamese, using the preferred language from the volunteer's profile.

### Fixed
- Shifts that cross midnight (e.g. the overnight shelter shift, 22:00-06:00) were shown on the wrong day in the weekly calendar.
- Names containing \* or \_ were rendered as emphasis in reminder emails.

## [3.2.0] - 2026-10-28

> [!WARNING]
> This release changes the **bookings API**. `GET /bookings` now returns a paginated object instead of a bare array, so partners using the Zapier integration must reconnect it.
> See the [migration notes](#migrating-from-31-to-32).

### Added
-   New _Kiosk mode_ for the sign-in tablets at the warehouse door.
    Volunteers tap their name and the kiosk records the check-in time.

    Kiosk mode needs a partner admin to enable it once per device:

    ```bash
    php artisan kiosk:register --organisation=12 --name="Warehouse door"
    ```
-   Organisations can set a minimum age per shift (`min_age`).
   - Shown on the shift card as "16+".
   - Enforced at booking time; younger volunteers can still sign up together with a guardian.
-   Calendar feeds (`.ics`) for each volunteer.

### Changed
1. Reminder emails are sent 24 hours before a shift instead of 48 (partners asked for this repeatedly).
1. The "My shifts" page now loads about three times faster for volunteers with long histories.
1. Dropped support for PHP 8.1.

### Fixed
* Cancelling a booking from the link in the reminder email didn't free the spot when the shift was in a different timezone than the server.
* Typo in the Vietnamese translation of "check in"  
  (thanks to Lan Pham for spotting it!)
* Organisation logos wider than 2000px broke the printable rota.\
  They are now scaled down on upload.

### Security
- Session cookies now use `SameSite=Lax`.
- Rate limiting on `/login`: 10 attempts per 15 minutes per IP address.

Migrating from 3.1 to 3.2
-------------------------

The bookings list endpoint changed shape. Before:

~~~json
[{"id": 1, "shift_id": 44, "status": "confirmed"}]
~~~

After:

```json
{"data": [{"id": 1, "shift_id": 44, "status": "confirmed"}], "next_cursor": null}
```

| Endpoint | 3.1 | 3.2 | Action needed |
|:---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `GET /bookings` | array | object (`data` + `next_cursor`) | update your client |
| `GET /shifts?status=open\|full` | yes | yes | none |
|`POST /bookings`|200|201| check the status code |

If you call the API from a spreadsheet (several food banks do this with Google Apps Script), the old behaviour is still available for six months by sending the header `Accept: application/vnd.shiftshare.v31+json`; after that it will be removed without further notice.

- - -

## [3.1.4] - 2026-08-19
### Fixed
- Volunteers who changed their email address were logged out on every device[^sessions].
- The waitlist promotion job ran twice when two shifts ended at the same minute.

## [3.1.0] - 2026-06-02 ##
### Added
3) Partner organisations can have more than one admin.
4) Bulk-create recurring shifts ("every Saturday until 31 August").

### Deprecated
- The `GET /v2/*` endpoints. They will be removed in 4.0, no earlier than __March 2027__.

<details>

--- title: Contributing to the library catalogue layout: default nav_order: 4 parent: "Developer guide" last_modified_date: 2026-10-02 tags: [koha, opac, contributing ] description: "How staff, volunteers and outside developers can propose changes to the Riverton Public Library catalogue: the OPAC theme, Koha plugins, MARC import rules and these docs." has_toc: False --- # Contributing to the Riverton Library catalogue # Thank you for helping! This repository contains everything that makes our catalogue look and behave the way it does: the OPAC theme, a handful of Koha plugins, the MARC import rules used by Technical Services, and the documentation you are reading. Contributions come from library staff, from volunteers in the *Tech Help Desk* program, and now and then from developers at other libraries that run Koha -- all of them are welcome. > [!IMPORTANT] > Never paste patron data (names, card numbers, addresses, borrowing history) into an issue, a pull request or a test fixture. Use the fake patrons in `t/fixtures/patrons.yml`. If you post real data by accident, tell the Library IT manager right away, because we have to report it within 72 hours. Ways to help ============ * **Report a problem.** Use the *Catalogue problem* issue template, and include the URL and what you expected to happen. * **Improve the docs.** Typos, unclear steps and missing screenshots are all fair game. + **Translate.** The OPAC is available in English, Spanish, Vietnamese and Arabic; we'd love Somali and Tagalog next. * **Write code.** See below. * Small fixes can go straight to a pull request. * Bigger changes: open an issue first so we can talk it through. * especially anything that touches circulation rules or fines Setting up a development environment ------------------------------------ You will need Docker and about 20 minutes. The community's `koha-testing-docker`[^ktd] project does most of the work: git clone https://gitlab.com/koha-community/koha-testing-docker.git cd koha-testing-docker cp env/defaults.env .env Then: 1. Set `SYNC_REPO` in `.env` to the path of your Koha clone. 1. Run `ktd up` and wait for the message *koha-testing-docker has started up and is ready to be enjoyed!* 1. Install our plugins: ```bash ./scripts/install-plugins.sh --instance kohadev --all ``` If the script complains that `Koha::Plugins` is not enabled, set `enable_plugins` to `1` in `koha-conf.xml` and restart Plack. 1. Open the OPAC at and the staff interface at .\ The default login is `koha` / `koha`. ### MARC import rules ### Import rules are small YAML files in `marc/rules/`, applied in file-name order to every record that arrives from a vendor. A typical rule looks like this: ```yaml # marc/rules/010-ebooks.yaml rule: ebooks-from-overdrive enabled: yes match: source: "OverDrive" leader_06: a actions: - add_field: {tag: "856", ind1: "4", ind2: "0", subfields: {u: "{{ record.url }}", z: "Read online with your library card"}} - set: { field: "942$c" , value: EBOOK } - delete_field: '9XX' ``` Use \_underscores\_ or hyphens in rule names, never spaces, and keep the numeric prefix so the order stays obvious. ## Pull requests > **Before you open a pull request**, check that: > > - the change has an issue (unless it's a typo fix) > - tests pass locally: `prove -r t/` > - for theme changes, also run `npm run lint:css` > - screenshots are attached for anything patrons will see > > A maintainer from Library IT will review it within a week. > [!TIP] > Draft pull requests are a good way to get early feedback. Nobody will merge a draft. Use this template for the description. It is also in `.github/pull_request_template.md`: ```markdown ## What does this change? Short summary. Link the issue, e.g. Fixes #123 ## How was it tested? * [ ] `prove -r t/` * [ ] Checked the OPAC with a screen reader (NVDA or VoiceOver) - [ ] Checked on a phone ``` ### Who reviews what | Area | Path | Reviewers | Staff sign-off? | Test command | Deploys to | Notes | |------|------|-----------|---|---|---|---| | OPAC theme | `opac/theme/` | M. Lopez, T. Khan | Yes (Branch Services) | `npm test` | catalogue.riverton.gov | Check colour contrast with the axe browser extension before asking for review | | Koha plugins | `plugins/` | T. Khan | No | `prove -r t/plugins` | staging, then production on Thursdays | Plugins must declare `minimum_version` | | MARC import rules | `marc/rules/*.yaml` | Technical Services | Yes | `./scripts/check-rules \| tee rules.log` | nightly import job | Rules run in file-name order | | Docs | `docs/` | anyone | No | `bundle exec jekyll build` | docs site | | Branch codes are used in plugin configuration and test fixtures. The table below is copied from the ILS admin screen, so please keep its layout as it is: | Branch | Code | Opened | |-------------|------|--------| | Central | CEN | 1911 | | St. Agnes | STA | 1958 | | Eastside |EAS | 1974 | | Bookmobile | BKM | 2019 | - - - ## Style notes * Perl follows the Koha coding guidelines; run `perltidy` with the project's `.perltidyrc`. * Templates use Template Toolkit. Keep logic out of them! * In the docs, write for a branch librarian, not for a developer: short sentences, *no* jargon, and spell out abbreviations the first time (OPAC = online public access catalogue). * Commit messages: `Bug 1234: Short description`, then a blank line, then a longer explanation if needed.
Why "Bug" even for features? Koha's own tooling expects that prefix, and we upstream some of our plugins.
It's a convention, not a judgement.
## Code of conduct Everyone taking part is expected to follow the Riverton Public Library [code of conduct][coc], which also applies in the library's meeting rooms and at events. Report problems to ; reports are read by two people outside Library IT. [^ktd]: koha-testing-docker is maintained by the Koha community, not by us. If it breaks after a Koha release, check the project's issue tracker before spending an afternoon debugging it. The people in the community chat are friendly and quick. [coc]: https://riverton-library.org/about/code-of-conduct [koha-guidelines]: https://wiki.koha-community.org/wiki/Coding_Guidelines [ktd-repo]: https://gitlab.com/koha-community/koha-testing-docker

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
source("R/load_quarterly.R")
q <- load_quarter(2026, 3)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to read this report
Each section starts with the key finding in **bold**. Figures are interactive in the HTML version; hover over a line to see the exact weekly count. Counts between 1 and 10 are suppressed, so some totals will not add up exactly.
:::

# Summary {#sec-summary}

**ILI activity started early this season.** In the third quarter there were `{r} format(q$ed_ili_total, big.mark = ",")` emergency department visits for influenza-like illness (ILI), compared with `{r} format(q$ed_ili_last_year, big.mark = ",")` in the same quarter of 2025 [@okafor2025; @cdc2024fluview, p. 4]. The increase was concentrated in the last three weeks of September (@fig-ili) and was largest among children aged 5 to 17.

Vaccination uptake is summarised in @tbl-vax. Clinic wait times improved at four of the six county clinics after the new online booking system launched in August[^booking], see @sec-methods for how waits are measured.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-ili
#| fig-cap: "Weekly ED visits for influenza-like illness, July to September 2026, compared with the five-season average"
#| fig-alt:   "Line chart showing weekly ILI visits rising sharply from week 36 onwards, well above the five-season average."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: '100%'
plot_ili(q$ili_weekly, baseline = q$ili_baseline)
```
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why the baseline changed
Before this quarter the baseline left out the 2020-21 and 2021-22 seasons. From Q3 2026 we use the five most recent complete seasons, as recommended by the state epidemiologist.
:::

-   ILI visits peaked in week 39.
-   Most visits were among school-age children.
    -  The North ZIP group had the highest rate.
-   Influenza A made up 72% of positive lab tests.
:::

::::

## Vaccination uptake {#sec-vax}

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Table

| Age group | Doses given | Uptake | Target |
|:----------|----:|:---:|---:|
| 6 months to 4 years | 1,204 | 31% | 50% |
| 5 to 17 | 3,980|28%|50%|
| 18 to 64 | 22,415 | 34% | 50% |
| 65 and over | 18,733 | 61% | 70% |

: Influenza vaccine doses given in Q3 2026, by age group. Uptake is cumulative since 1 July. {#tbl-vax}

### Chart

```{r}
#| label: fig-vax
#| fig-cap: Cumulative uptake by age group
#| fig-alt: Bar chart of cumulative influenza vaccine uptake by age group compared with the targets.
#| column: page-right
plot_uptake(q$vax, targets = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.7))
```
:::

::: callout-warning
Uptake for the 65 and over group is **9 points below target**. Pharmacies report doses to the state registry with a delay of up to three weeks, so the final figure will be somewhat higher, but probably not high enough to reach 70%.
:::

## Clinic wait times

![Location of the six county clinics and the four ZIP code groups](figures/clinic-map.png){#fig-map width="70%" fig-align="center" fig-alt="Map of Riverton County showing six clinic locations spread across four ZIP code groups."}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-wait
#| tbl-cap: "Median wait in days for a first appointment, by clinic and month"
#| fmt: skip
#| tbl-colwidths: [40,20,20,20]
wait_table(q$waits) |> gt::fmt_number(decimals = 0)
```

The longest waits remain at the Millbrook clinic (@fig-map), which has had one vacant nurse practitioner post since May. Waits at Eastside fell from 19 days in July to 8 days in September.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

Weekly rates are calculated per 100,000 residents:

$$
r_{w,g} = \frac{c_{w,g}}{P_g} \times 100{,}000
$$

where $c_{w,g}$ is the number of visits in week $w$ for ZIP group $g$, and $P_g$ is the 2025 population estimate. Confidence intervals for small counts use the method of Fay and Feuer [@fay1997].

### Definitions

Influenza-like illness (ILI)
:   Fever of 100°F or higher **and** a cough or sore throat, without a known cause other than influenza.

Provisional
: A count for the two most recent weeks. Provisional counts usually rise by 5-15% as late records arrive, so don't compare them directly with final counts.

Wait time
:    The number of days between a booking request and the first available appointment at the requested clinic, measured on the first Monday of each month.

::: {.callout-important title="Data quality"}
ED data for 9 to 12 August are incomplete because of an outage at the state feed. Those days are excluded from @fig-ili, and the weekly totals for week 32 were imputed from the surrounding weeks.
:::

[^booking]: The booking system was funded by a one-off state grant, which ends in June 2027.

    Whether the county continues to pay for it will be decided in the 2027-28 budget. Clinic managers have asked for the decision to be made before the winter peak.

title: "Summer Reading Challenge 2026: Evaluation Report"
author:   "Dr. Priya Raman (Evaluation Unit) and the Youth Services team"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%B %d, %Y')`"
output:
  html_document:
     toc: true
     toc_float: yes
     number_sections: false
     df_print: kable
  word_document: default
params:
  year: 2026
  branches: [Central, "St. Agnes", Eastside, Millbrook, "North Riverton", Bookmobile]
bibliography: srp-references.bib
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console
  markdown:
      wrap: sentence
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
srp <- read_csv("data/srp_2026_registrations.csv")
n_reg <- nrow(srp)
n_finished <- sum(srp$finished)
pct_finished <- round(100 * n_finished / n_reg)
n_books <- sum(srp$books_logged)
```

# Summary

The 2026 Summer Reading Challenge ran from June 8 to August 15 at all six locations of the Riverton Public Library, i.e. Central, St. Agnes, Eastside, Millbrook, North Riverton and the Bookmobile. In total `r format(n_reg, big.mark = ",")` children and teens registered, and `r pct_finished`% of them finished the challenge. That is the highest completion rate since the program was redesigned in 2021. Registrations at the St. Agnes branch nearly doubled vs. last year (see Fig. 3), which staff put down to the new partnership with St. Agnes Elementary School. Did the shorter ten-book goal make the difference? We think it helped, but it is not the whole story...

Participants logged approx. `r format(n_books, big.mark = ",")` books, or about 14 per finisher. The median finisher read on 22 of the 69 days. Teens (ages 13 to 18) remain the hardest group to reach: only 312 registered, compared with 1,940 children aged 5 to 12.

## Background and aims

The challenge has three aims, set by the Library Board in 2019. First, to slow the "summer slide" in reading skills [@cooper1996; @kim2004]. Second, to bring families who don't usually use the library through the door. Third, to give branch staff a reason to talk with young readers about what they enjoy.

As Dr. Raman put it at the June board meeting, "We are not trying to make kids read more pages. We want them to want to read." This report asks whether the 2026 design moved us towards those aims, e.g. by looking at repeat visits, first-time library card sign-ups and the share of finishers from priority neighbourhoods. (Priority neighbourhoods are defined in the 2024 strategic plan.) Where possible we compare with 2025, but the two years are not directly comparable because the registration form changed in May.

## What changed in 2026?

* **A shorter goal.** The goal dropped from 15 books to 10, and audiobooks, graphic novels and books read aloud by a parent all counted. Several parents told us this was the first year their child felt the goal was "actually doable."
* **Paper logs are back.** In 2025 the challenge was online only. This excluded families without reliable internet access, which Ms. Okonkwo at the Eastside branch flagged in her end-of-summer report. Paper logs were offered at every branch and on the Bookmobile.
*   **School partnerships.** Librarians visited 11 elementary schools in May (vs. 4 in 2025). Each visit took approx. 40 minutes, incl. a short booktalk and a registration table.
    Visits were concentrated in the St. Agnes and Millbrook catchment areas.
* **Prizes.** Finishers received a free book rather than a voucher for a fast-food restaurant. Was that a risk? Some staff thought so.

```{r registrations-by-branch, fig.cap="Fig. 3: Registrations by branch, 2025 vs. 2026."}
#| fig.alt: "Grouped bar chart comparing registrations at six library locations in 2025 and 2026."
#| out.width:   '90%'
#| dev: [png, pdf]
srp |>
  count(branch, year) |>
  ggplot(aes(branch, n, fill = factor(year))) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Registrations", fill = NULL)
```

## Findings

### Completion

Completion rose at every location except the Bookmobile, where it fell from 41% to 37%. The Bookmobile figures are based on paper logs collected at the last stop of each route, so they probably undercount finishers. (Some families finished the challenge but never returned their log.) Story time attendance was also up; the 10 a.m. sessions at Central were full on most weekdays in July.

> Several branch managers made the same point in their reports. Children who visited at least four times were far more likely to finish. Visits, not prizes, seem to drive completion. Should next year's design reward visits directly?

### New library cards

A total of 486 first-time library cards were issued to challenge participants, up from 301 in 2025. Most of the increase came from the school visits; children who registered at school were twice as likely to get their first card during the summer. Is this effect likely to last? We will check the 2027 circulation data before drawing conclusions.

```{r new-cards, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
#| tbl-cap: New library cards issued to challenge participants, by branch.
#| tbl-colwidths:   [50, 25, 25]
srp |>
  filter(new_card) |>
  count(branch, name = "new_cards") |>
  arrange(desc(new_cards)) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Branch", "New cards"))
```

## Recommendations

1. Keep the ten-book goal and the broad definition of "a book." Do not go back to the 15-book goal without testing it first.
1. Expand school visits to all 23 elementary schools in the county, starting with those in priority neighbourhoods. This will need approx. 60 hours of librarian time in May.
1. Pilot a "visit passport" at two branches, e.g. Eastside and Millbrook. Children would get a stamp for each visit. Would that help teens too? Probably not, so...
1. Work with the Teen Advisory Board on a separate design for ages 13 to 18. Their ideas so far include a book-to-film club and volunteering hours.

## Limitations

This evaluation relies on registration data and staff reports. We did not measure reading skills directly, i.e. we cannot say whether the challenge reduced summer learning loss. Paper and online logs are not equivalent either: the online form asks for titles, the paper log only for a tally. Finally, response rates to the parent survey were low (n = 214, approx. 9% of registrants), so the survey results in Appendix B should be read with care.

<!-- TODO(youth services): add the Appendix B survey tables once the Spanish responses are translated. -->

# References
